note: Islamic Religious Studies round 3 (part B): the life of the Prophet, the Hijrah, the Prophet as leader and model, the Rightly Guided Caliphs, the Madinan community, family life, marriage and divorce, parents and children, brotherhood, justice, honesty, corruption, economic principles, lawful and unlawful, political administration, shura, relations with non-Muslims, Islamic history and expansion, contemporary issues.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) belonged to the clan of Banu Hashim of the tribe of
questions.A: Aws
questions.B: Quraysh
questions.C: Khazraj
questions.D: Thaqif
questions.explanation: The Quraysh were custodians of the Ka'bah in Makkah; Aws and Khazraj were the tribes of Madinah; Thaqif of Ta'if.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: After the death of his mother, the young Muhammad (SAW) was cared for first by his grandfather Abdul-Muttalib and then by his uncle
questions.A: Hamzah
questions.B: Abu Lahab
questions.C: Abu Talib
questions.D: Abbas
questions.explanation: Abu Talib raised him and protected him after prophethood until his death in the Year of Sorrow.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: As a young man Muhammad (SAW) joined an alliance of Makkan clans pledged to defend the wronged and oppressed. This pact was
questions.A: the Pledge of Aqabah
questions.B: the Constitution of Madinah
questions.C: the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
questions.D: Hilf al-Fudul
questions.explanation: Hilf al-Fudul (the League of the Virtuous) was formed to protect strangers and the weak in Makkah; the Prophet later praised it.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) received his first revelation at the age of
questions.A: twenty-five
questions.B: forty
questions.C: fifty-three
questions.D: sixty-three
questions.explanation: He was 40 at the first revelation, 53 at the Hijrah and 63 at his death.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: After the first revelation, Khadijah took the Prophet (SAW) to her Christian cousin, who confirmed that the being he had seen was the same who came to Musa. That cousin was
questions.A: Umayyah ibn Khalaf
questions.B: Abu Sufyan
questions.C: Waraqah ibn Nawfal
questions.D: Suhayl ibn Amr
questions.explanation: Waraqah, learned in the scriptures, recognised the Namus (Jibril) and warned that his people would drive him out.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: For about three years the Prophet (SAW) preached secretly. Among the first to accept Islam were his wife Khadijah, his cousin Ali, his freed slave Zayd and his friend
questions.A: Khalid ibn al-Walid
questions.B: Umar
questions.C: Uthman
questions.D: Abu Bakr
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr was the first free adult man to accept Islam and brought in Uthman, Talhah, Zubayr and others.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: When the persecution of weak Muslims such as Bilal and the family of Yasir became severe, the Prophet (SAW) advised some of them to migrate to
questions.A: Ta'if, to seek the protection of Thaqif
questions.B: Abyssinia (Habashah), ruled by a just Christian king
questions.C: Yemen, to trade with the Persians
questions.D: Syria, to live among the monks
questions.explanation: The first Hijrah to Abyssinia (5th year of prophethood) was to the Negus (Najashi), who refused to hand the Muslims over.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Before the Negus, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib described the condition of the Arabs before Islam and how the Prophet changed them. He said the Prophet commanded them to
questions.A: worship the sun and the moon and offer sacrifices to them at the Ka'bah
questions.B: conquer Abyssinia, expel the Christians and seize the treasures of the Negus
questions.C: speak the truth, keep trusts, honour kinship and abandon idols and immorality
questions.D: trade only with the Quraysh of Makkah and refuse all dealings with strangers
questions.explanation: Ja'far's speech summarised the moral revolution of Islam and won the Negus's protection.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Quraysh boycotted Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib for about three years, confining them to a valley and refusing to trade or intermarry with them. This boycott ended when
questions.A: the Muslims defeated the Quraysh at Badr and forced them to lift the siege
questions.B: the Prophet agreed to stop preaching in public in exchange for food supplies
questions.C: the Negus of Abyssinia sent an army to Makkah to rescue the Banu Hashim
questions.D: the document of boycott was found eaten by termites except the name of Allah
questions.explanation: The boycott in Shi'b Abi Talib ended in the 10th year of prophethood after several Quraysh leaders moved to annul it.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: During the Isra' and Mi'raj the Prophet (SAW) was taken by night from Makkah to
questions.A: the city of Madinah and then to the town of Ta'if
questions.B: Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem and then through the heavens
questions.C: the court of the Negus in Abyssinia and then to Yemen
questions.D: the top of Mount Uhud and then to the wells of Badr
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Isra' 17:1 mentions the journey to the Farthest Mosque; from there he ascended through the heavens.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: At the second Pledge of Aqabah, about 73 people from Yathrib pledged to
questions.A: build a fortress at Ta'if where the Muslims of Makkah could take refuge
questions.B: pay a yearly tribute of camels and dates to the Quraysh in exchange for peace
questions.C: protect the Prophet (SAW) as they protected their own families if he migrated to them
questions.D: send their sons to Makkah to study the scriptures under the rabbis of the city
questions.explanation: The pledge of war/protection at Aqabah opened the way for the Hijrah to Madinah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) died in Madinah in the year
questions.B: 1 AH (622 CE)
questions.C: 8 AH (630 CE)
questions.explanation: He died on 12 Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH in the apartment of A'ishah and was buried there.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: When the Prophet (SAW) died, Umar refused to believe it until Abu Bakr recited the verse
questions.A: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' (96:1)
questions.B: 'Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him' (3:144)
questions.C: 'Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory' (48:1)
questions.D: 'When the help of Allah comes and the victory' (110:1)
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr said: 'Whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad is dead; whoever worships Allah, Allah is Ever-Living.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) received the title 'al-Amin' (the trustworthy) from the Makkans because
questions.A: he was the strongest wrestler in the city
questions.B: he was the richest merchant in Makkah
questions.C: he never lied or betrayed a trust even before prophethood
questions.D: he had memorised the poems of the Arabs
questions.explanation: His honesty in trade and daily life earned him this title long before revelation.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Before prophethood, Muhammad (SAW) accompanied his uncle Abu Talib on a trade journey to Syria, where a monk recognised signs of prophethood in him. The monk was
questions.A: Suhayb
questions.B: Waraqah
questions.C: Salman
questions.D: Bahira
questions.explanation: The monk Bahira at Busra advised Abu Talib to guard the boy from the Jews.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet's (SAW) marriage to Khadijah lasted about twenty-five years. During her lifetime he
questions.A: married four other wives
questions.B: married no other woman
questions.C: divorced her twice
questions.D: lived in Madinah
questions.explanation: Khadijah was his only wife until her death in the tenth year of prophethood.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The period between the first revelation and the second is called the fatrah. During it the Prophet (SAW)
questions.A: built the mosque at Quba and the mosque of Madinah with the help of the Ansar
questions.B: led the Muslim army to the conquest of Makkah and cleansed the Ka'bah of its idols
questions.C: was distressed by the pause until Surah Al-Muddaththir was revealed commanding him to arise and warn
questions.D: signed the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah with the Quraysh and returned to Madinah in peace
questions.explanation: The pause in revelation ended with 'O you wrapped in garments, arise and warn' (74:1-2).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Hijrah refers to the migration of the Prophet (SAW) and his companions from
questions.A: Ta'if to Makkah in 619 CE
questions.B: Madinah to Makkah in 630 CE
questions.C: Makkah to Abyssinia in 615 CE
questions.D: Makkah to Madinah in 622 CE
questions.explanation: The migration to Yathrib (Madinah) in 622 CE marks the start of the Islamic calendar.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Quraysh decided that a young man from each clan should strike the Prophet (SAW) together so that his blood would be spread among all clans. The Qur'an refers to this plot in the verse
questions.A: 'Fasting is prescribed for you' (2:183)
questions.B: 'And when the disbelievers plotted against you to confine you, kill you or expel you' (8:30)
questions.C: 'And establish prayer at the two ends of the day' (11:114)
questions.D: 'Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship' (109:1-2)
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Anfal 8:30 recalls the plot and adds 'they plan, and Allah plans, and Allah is the best of planners'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: When the pursuers reached the mouth of the cave of Thawr, Abu Bakr feared they would be seen. The Prophet (SAW) said:
questions.A: 'Go, for you are free'
questions.B: 'Fight them until there is no persecution'
questions.C: 'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us' (9:40)
questions.D: 'Read in the name of your Lord'
questions.explanation: The Qur'an records the words in Surah At-Tawbah 9:40 and mentions the tranquillity Allah sent down.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Abu Bakr's daughter, who secretly brought food to the cave and tore her waist-band to tie the provisions, earning the title 'Dhat an-Nitaqayn', was
questions.A: Umm Salamah
questions.B: A'ishah
questions.C: Fatimah
questions.D: Asma'
questions.explanation: Asma' bint Abi Bakr supported the Hijrah; her brother Abdullah brought news and their servant Amir ibn Fuhayrah erased the tracks with sheep.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The guide hired to lead the Prophet (SAW) and Abu Bakr to Madinah by an unfamiliar route was a non-Muslim named
questions.A: Suraqah ibn Malik
questions.B: Abdullah ibn Urayqit
questions.C: Abu Jahl
questions.D: Umayyah ibn Khalaf
questions.explanation: Ibn Urayqit, though a polytheist, was trusted to keep the secret and guide them along the coast.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Suraqah ibn Malik pursued the Prophet (SAW) for the Quraysh reward but his horse sank in the sand repeatedly. He then
questions.A: joined the Prophet immediately and migrated with him
questions.B: captured the Prophet and returned him to Makkah
questions.C: asked for a guarantee of safety and turned back, keeping the pursuers away
questions.D: sent a message to the Negus
questions.explanation: The Prophet promised Suraqah the bracelets of the Persian emperor, a promise fulfilled under Umar.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: On arrival in Madinah, the site of the Prophet's mosque was chosen where
questions.A: the Jewish leaders had their council, on land bought by Abu Bakr
questions.B: the largest palm grove stood, on land donated by Abdullah ibn Ubayy
questions.C: the market of Banu Qaynuqa' was located, on land seized from the Jews
questions.D: his she-camel knelt, on land belonging to two orphans which he paid for
questions.explanation: The Prophet insisted on paying the orphans Sahl and Suhayl for the land where Qaswa' stopped.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The people of Madinah who welcomed and supported the emigrants were called the Ansar, while the emigrants themselves were called
questions.A: the Munafiqun
questions.B: the Muhajirun
questions.C: the Quraysh
questions.D: the Ahl al-Kitab
questions.explanation: Muhajirun means emigrants; Ansar means helpers.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Hijrah is significant in Islamic history because it
questions.A: was the year in which the revelation of the whole Qur'an was completed
questions.B: ended all conflict between the Muslims and the Quraysh once and for all
questions.C: turned the persecuted Muslims into an organised community with its own state
questions.D: changed the direction of prayer from the Ka'bah to Jerusalem for ever
questions.explanation: In Madinah the Prophet founded a state, a mosque and a constitution, and Islam spread rapidly.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim leaves a place where he is unable to practise his faith and moves to where he can. The Prophet (SAW) said, 'The muhajir is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.' The lesson is that Hijrah in its wider sense means
questions.A: refusing to work in a non-Muslim country
questions.B: travelling every year to Madinah
questions.C: abandoning one's family
questions.D: leaving sin and disobedience for obedience to Allah
questions.explanation: Physical migration for faith is one form; the inner hijrah from sin is required of every Muslim.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: When the companions debated whether the Muslim calendar should start from the Prophet's birth, the first revelation, the Hijrah or his death, Umar chose the Hijrah because
questions.A: it was the only date that the companions could remember exactly
questions.B: it marked the turning point at which the Muslims became a free and organised community
questions.C: the Prophet had written the date of the Hijrah in the Qur'an
questions.D: the Christians and the Persians also began their calendars from that year
questions.explanation: In about 17 AH Umar, after consultation, fixed the Hijrah as the epoch because it separated the era of persecution from the era of the Muslim state.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Lessons that a Muslim student can learn from the planning of the Hijrah include
questions.A: that one should never accept help from a non-Muslim
questions.B: that success comes without any effort or preparation
questions.C: combining trust in Allah with careful planning and use of lawful means
questions.D: that secrecy is forbidden in Islam
questions.explanation: The Prophet planned the route, guide, provisions and informant, yet relied wholly on Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Ali ibn Abi Talib remained in Makkah for a few days after the Hijrah in order to
questions.A: collect the Zakat of the Makkan Muslims and carry it to Madinah
questions.B: sell the Prophet's house and camels and bring the money to Madinah
questions.C: fight the Quraysh youths who had surrounded the Prophet's house
questions.D: return the trusts (deposits) that the Makkans had left with the Prophet (SAW)
questions.explanation: Even while plotting to kill him, the Makkans kept their valuables with al-Amin; Ali returned them.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: After the battle of Badr, the Prophet (SAW) allowed literate prisoners of war to gain their freedom by
questions.A: paying gold equal to their weight
questions.B: teaching ten Muslim children to read and write
questions.C: converting to Islam by force
questions.D: serving as soldiers in the Muslim army
questions.explanation: This decision shows his concern for education and humane treatment of prisoners.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: At the battle of Badr, a young companion suggested that the Muslims camp at the nearest well and block the others. The Prophet (SAW) accepted the advice, showing that as a leader he
questions.A: made decisions only through revelation
questions.B: never took advice from anyone
questions.C: consulted others and accepted good counsel regardless of rank
questions.D: punished those who suggested alternatives
questions.explanation: Al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir asked whether the position was by revelation or opinion; the Prophet adopted his plan.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: When a companion asked the Prophet (SAW) for a position of authority, he replied: 'We do not appoint to this work anyone who asks for it or is eager for it.' This teaches that leadership in Islam
questions.A: is inherited from father to son like the kingship of Persia and Byzantium
questions.B: should be given to whoever asks for it first and shows the most eagerness
questions.C: belongs only to members of the Quraysh and their descendants for all time
questions.D: is a trust to be given to the competent, not sought for personal ambition
questions.explanation: The Hadith (Bukhari and Muslim) discourages seeking office for its own sake.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: In dividing the spoils of Hunayn, the Prophet (SAW) gave generously to the new Makkan converts and little to the Ansar. When the Ansar complained, he
questions.A: punished them for questioning his decision and sent them back to Madinah without any share
questions.B: explained his reasons and reminded them that they would return home with the Messenger of Allah
questions.C: took back the gifts he had given to the Makkans and divided them equally among the Ansar
questions.D: expelled them from Madinah and gave their houses and farms to the new Makkan converts
questions.explanation: His speech to the Ansar shows a leader who explains, reassures and wins hearts.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) sent letters inviting rulers such as Heraclius, Chosroes and the Negus to Islam. This shows that as a leader he
questions.A: ignored the world outside Arabia and preached to the Arabs only
questions.B: relied only on military force to make the rulers accept Islam
questions.C: used diplomacy and peaceful invitation to spread the message
questions.D: sought military alliances with the idolaters against the Christians
questions.explanation: The letters after Hudaybiyyah carried the universal message of Islam to foreign courts.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: At the digging of the trench before the siege of Madinah, the Prophet (SAW)
questions.A: hired labourers from the Jewish tribes to dig the trench
questions.B: supervised the work from a tent pitched on Mount Sal'
questions.C: left Madinah for Makkah to negotiate with the Quraysh
questions.D: carried earth and broke rocks alongside the companions
questions.explanation: His sharing of hard labour raised the companions' morale and showed leadership by example.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: When the Prophet (SAW) entered Makkah as a conqueror in 8 AH, he entered
questions.A: on a golden throne carried on the shoulders of the captured Quraysh chiefs
questions.B: with his head bowed low on his camel in humility and gratitude to Allah
questions.C: with drums and dancing and the singing girls of Madinah before him
questions.D: after burning the houses of his enemies and seizing their wealth
questions.explanation: His humility in victory contrasted with the arrogance of worldly conquerors.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) appointed Usamah ibn Zayd, a youth of about eighteen, to command an army that included senior companions. This shows that in his leadership
questions.A: commands were sold to the highest bidder
questions.B: only elders were given command
questions.C: merit and ability counted more than age or lineage
questions.D: the Quraysh alone could lead
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr later dispatched Usamah's army as the Prophet had ordered.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: In the Farewell Sermon the Prophet (SAW) declared: 'All the practices of the days of ignorance are under my feet; the blood-feuds of jahiliyyah are abolished, and usury is abolished.' The first usury he cancelled was that of
questions.A: the traders of the tribe of Thaqif in Ta'if
questions.B: the Makkan chief Abu Sufyan ibn Harb
questions.C: the Jewish merchants of Khaybar
questions.D: his own uncle Abbas ibn Abdul-Muttalib
questions.explanation: He began reform with his own family, showing impartial leadership.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: As head of state in Madinah, the Prophet (SAW) received delegations, signed treaties, appointed governors and judges, and organised Zakat collection. This shows that Islam
questions.A: is concerned only with private worship and the affairs of the mosque
questions.B: does not separate religion from the organisation of society and the state
questions.C: forbids Muslims from holding any public office or political position
questions.D: requires a king chosen by the Quraysh to rule over all the Muslims
questions.explanation: The Prophet was both spiritual guide and political leader of the community.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: Before the battle of Uhud, the Prophet (SAW) preferred to defend from within Madinah, but the majority of the companions wanted to go out. He
questions.A: cancelled the battle and sent messengers to the Quraysh asking for peace
questions.B: insisted on his own view and ordered the companions to stay in the city
questions.C: went out to meet the enemy, following the majority after consultation
questions.D: asked the Jewish tribes of Madinah to decide the matter between them
questions.explanation: He put on his armour and would not remove it once decided, teaching firmness after consultation.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'The leader of a people is their servant.' A Nigerian governor who applies this teaching would
questions.A: keep the public funds of the state for his own use and that of his family
questions.B: expect the people of the state to serve his family and his friends
questions.C: refuse to attend to the complaints of the poor people of the state
questions.D: use his office to serve the citizens rather than to enrich himself
questions.explanation: Islamic leadership is service and accountability, not privilege.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: The Qur'an says: 'Indeed in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example (uswah hasanah)' (33:21). This means Muslims should
questions.A: worship the Prophet alongside Allah and pray to him for their needs
questions.B: imitate the Prophet's character and conduct in their own lives
questions.C: read only the biography of the Prophet and leave the rest of the Qur'an
questions.D: wear the Arab dress of the seventh century at all times and in all places
questions.explanation: The Prophet's life is the practical model of Islam for every believer.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: When asked about the Prophet's character, A'ishah replied: 'His character was the Qur'an.' She meant that he
questions.A: read the Qur'an aloud all day long in the mosque of Madinah
questions.B: had memorised the whole Qur'an from beginning to end
questions.C: lived out the teachings of the Qur'an in his daily conduct
questions.D: wrote the Qur'an himself with the help of his companions
questions.explanation: His behaviour embodied the commands and virtues of the Qur'an.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: A woman used to throw rubbish on the Prophet (SAW) whenever he passed her house. When she fell ill and stopped, he
questions.A: avoided her street for ever
questions.B: sent men to destroy her house
questions.C: cursed her family
questions.D: visited her to ask after her health
questions.explanation: His kindness to those who harmed him is a model of forbearance.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'The best of you are the best to their families, and I am the best of you to my family.' A husband who helps with housework and is gentle with his wife is
questions.A: acting against Islamic manhood
questions.B: following the Prophet's example at home
questions.C: committing bid'ah
questions.D: neglecting his religion
questions.explanation: The Prophet served his household, mended his sandals and played with children.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: A Bedouin urinated in the mosque and the companions rushed to stop him. The Prophet (SAW) told them to leave him, then had water poured over the spot and gently explained. This teaches
questions.A: that punishment must be immediate and harsh
questions.B: that the mosque may be used for any purpose
questions.C: gentleness and wisdom in correcting the ignorant
questions.D: that Bedouins are not welcome in the mosque
questions.explanation: The Prophet said he was sent to make things easy, not difficult.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) accepted invitations from slaves and the poor, sat on the ground and ate with servants. This is an example of his
questions.A: eloquence in speech
questions.B: generosity in wealth
questions.C: bravery in battle
questions.D: humility (tawadu')
questions.explanation: His humility contrasted with the pride of the Arab chiefs.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: During the battle of Hunayn, when many Muslims fled at the first ambush, the Prophet (SAW)
questions.A: fled with them to Makkah and waited there until the Hawazin had withdrawn
questions.B: stood firm on his mule and called them back, saying 'I am the Prophet without lie'
questions.C: surrendered to the Hawazin and agreed to pay them a ransom for the prisoners
questions.D: hid in a cave on the mountain until Abu Bakr arrived with fresh troops
questions.explanation: His courage rallied the Muslims to victory; Ali said the companions sheltered behind the Prophet when fighting grew fierce.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: A merchant in Kano who gives full measure, points out defects in his goods and keeps his word to customers is imitating the Prophet (SAW) in
questions.A: leadership of the congregational prayer
questions.B: strategy and tactics in warfare
questions.C: honesty and trustworthiness in trade
questions.D: performance of the rites of pilgrimage
questions.explanation: The Prophet was a truthful trader before and after prophethood.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) never took revenge for himself, but when the limits of Allah were violated he
questions.A: punished only the poor and pardoned the rich and powerful
questions.B: forgave every crime and left the offender without punishment
questions.C: left the punishment to the tribes and their customary law
questions.D: enforced the law without regard to the offender's status
questions.explanation: A'ishah said he never avenged himself unless the sanctity of Allah was violated.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: The Prophet's (SAW) treatment of children included
questions.A: forbidding them from entering the mosque or attending the congregational prayer
questions.B: greeting them, playing with them and carrying his grandchildren during prayer
questions.C: beating them severely for small mistakes so that they would learn discipline
questions.D: ignoring them in public so that the adults would not think less of him
questions.explanation: He shortened prayer when a child cried and let Hasan and Husayn ride on his back.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) often went hungry, tied stones to his stomach and slept on a rough mat that left marks on his side, though he could have lived in luxury. This models
questions.A: the prohibition of wealth in Islam
questions.B: poverty as a religious requirement for all
questions.C: simplicity and detachment from worldly excess (zuhd)
questions.D: the rejection of all comfort
questions.explanation: Zuhd is contentment with little and freedom from greed, not the prohibition of lawful wealth.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said, 'I was sent only to perfect good character.' A Muslim who studies the Sirah should therefore aim to
questions.A: imitate the dress and food of seventh-century Arabia in every detail
questions.B: memorise the dates of the battles and the names of the companions only
questions.C: learn the names of the Prophet's camels, horses and swords by heart
questions.D: acquire the Prophet's virtues of truthfulness, mercy, patience and justice
questions.explanation: The purpose of studying his life is moral transformation.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Abu Bakr was chosen as the first caliph at the meeting held at
questions.A: the cave of Hira
questions.B: Saqifah of Banu Sa'idah
questions.C: the plain of Arafat
questions.D: the mosque of Quba
questions.explanation: At the Saqifah the Ansar and Muhajirun agreed on Abu Bakr after Umar pledged allegiance to him.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Abu Bakr was called 'as-Siddiq' (the truthful, the one who confirms) because he
questions.A: compiled the scattered pages of the Qur'an into one volume after the battle of Yamamah
questions.B: fought with great courage at the battle of Yamamah against the false prophet Musaylimah
questions.C: immediately believed the Prophet's account of the Isra' and Mi'raj when others doubted
questions.D: founded the city of Basrah in Iraq and built its first mosque with his own money
questions.explanation: When the Quraysh mocked the Night Journey, Abu Bakr said: 'If he said it, it is true.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The false prophet Musaylimah was defeated and killed at the battle of Yamamah during the caliphate of
questions.A: Ali
questions.B: Umar
questions.C: Uthman
questions.D: Abu Bakr
questions.explanation: The Riddah wars under Abu Bakr crushed apostasy and false prophets, including Musaylimah killed by Wahshi.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Umar ibn al-Khattab was given the title 'al-Faruq', meaning
questions.A: the possessor of two lights from the Prophet
questions.B: the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood
questions.C: the drawn sword of Allah against His enemies
questions.D: the trusted keeper of the wealth of the ummah
questions.explanation: Umar's conversion openly separated truth from falsehood in Makkah; Uthman was Dhun-Nurayn; Khalid was Sayfullah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Umar used to patrol Madinah at night to see the condition of the people. One night he heard a mother boiling water with stones to quiet her hungry children. He
questions.A: sent her and her children to Makkah to live with her relatives
questions.B: ordered her arrest for complaining publicly against the caliph
questions.C: personally carried a sack of flour from the treasury to her house
questions.D: ignored the matter and continued his patrol of the city
questions.explanation: The story illustrates Umar's sense of responsibility: 'How shall I answer Allah for them?'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Jerusalem surrendered to the Muslims in 15/16 AH and Caliph Umar travelled to receive it. He granted its Christians a covenant that
questions.A: imposed slavery on the inhabitants
questions.B: ordered the conversion of all churches into mosques
questions.C: expelled all Christians from the city
questions.D: guaranteed the safety of their lives, churches and crosses
questions.explanation: The Pact of Umar with Patriarch Sophronius protected the Christians of Jerusalem.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Umar was assassinated while leading the Fajr prayer by
questions.A: Ibn Muljam, a Khariji
questions.B: Abu Lu'lu'ah, a Persian slave
questions.C: a soldier of the Quraysh
questions.D: a Jewish merchant of Khaybar
questions.explanation: Abu Lu'lu'ah (Firoz) stabbed Umar in 23 AH; Ibn Muljam killed Ali in 40 AH.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Before his death, Umar appointed a committee of six companions to choose his successor. The committee chose
questions.A: Talhah ibn Ubaydullah
questions.B: Ali ibn Abi Talib
questions.C: Uthman ibn Affan
questions.D: Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf
questions.explanation: Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf consulted the people and the committee settled on Uthman in 23/24 AH.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Uthman was called 'Dhun-Nurayn' (possessor of two lights) because he
questions.A: compiled two complete copies of the Qur'an with his own hand
questions.B: built two great mosques in Madinah and lit them with lamps at night
questions.C: led the two migrations of the Muslims to Abyssinia and back to Makkah
questions.D: married two daughters of the Prophet (SAW), Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum
questions.explanation: After Ruqayyah's death he married her sister Umm Kulthum.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: During his caliphate Uthman expanded the Prophet's mosque, built a navy that won the Battle of the Masts, and
questions.A: moved the capital of the caliphate from Madinah to Damascus in Syria
questions.B: standardised the Qur'anic text and sent official copies to the main cities
questions.C: abolished the Bayt al-Mal and distributed all its wealth among the people
questions.D: ended the conquest of Persia and withdrew the Muslim armies to Arabia
questions.explanation: The Uthmanic mushaf preserved a single authoritative text of the Qur'an.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Uthman was killed in 35 AH by
questions.A: the Byzantine army at the battle of Yarmuk on the border of Syria
questions.B: the Persian army at the battle of Nahavand in the mountains of Iran
questions.C: rebels who besieged his house in Madinah while he was reading the Qur'an
questions.D: the Kharijites at the battle of Nahrawan on the banks of the Tigris
questions.explanation: Discontented groups from Egypt, Kufah and Basrah besieged and murdered the aged caliph.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The battle of the Camel (36 AH) was fought between the forces of Ali and those led by
questions.A: the Persian nobles of Ctesiphon, who wanted to restore the Sasanian throne
questions.B: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, the governor of Syria, and his army from Damascus
questions.C: the Kharijites of Nahrawan, who had rejected the arbitration at Siffin
questions.D: A'ishah, Talhah and Zubayr, who demanded punishment of Uthman's killers
questions.explanation: The battle took its name from the camel on which A'ishah sat; Talhah and Zubayr were killed.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: At the battle of Siffin (37 AH), Mu'awiyah's soldiers raised copies of the Qur'an on their lances to call for
questions.A: the immediate surrender of Ali
questions.B: arbitration (tahkim) instead of continued fighting
questions.C: the return of the capital to Madinah
questions.D: the release of the prisoners of Badr
questions.explanation: Ali accepted arbitration, which led a group of his followers (the Khawarij) to secede.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Khawarij (Kharijites) were a group who
questions.A: were the Jewish tribes of Madinah who broke the covenant with the Prophet
questions.B: supported Mu'awiyah from the very beginning and fought for him against Ali
questions.C: rejected the arbitration at Siffin, declaring that judgement belongs to Allah alone
questions.D: were the companions who fled at Uhud and were later forgiven by the Prophet
questions.explanation: Their slogan 'la hukma illa lillah' masked extremism; one of them later murdered Ali.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was raised in the Prophet's household and married his daughter Fatimah, was known for
questions.A: his role as the Prophet's chief scribe who wrote down every verse of the Qur'an as it was revealed
questions.B: his enormous wealth as the richest merchant of Makkah, whose caravans travelled to Syria and Yemen
questions.C: his refusal to take part in any battle fought by the Muslims because he hated bloodshed
questions.D: his knowledge, courage and eloquence; the Prophet said 'I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate'
questions.explanation: Ali fought at Badr, Uhud and Khaybar and was famed for judicial wisdom.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A key administrative achievement common to the Rightly Guided Caliphs was that they
questions.A: made the caliphate hereditary within one family so that succession disputes would be avoided
questions.B: consulted the companions (shura) and regarded themselves as accountable servants of the people
questions.C: moved the capital of the Islamic state from Madinah to Baghdad on the banks of the Tigris
questions.D: abolished the payment of Zakat and replaced it with a land tax on all Muslims and non-Muslims
questions.explanation: Government by consultation and accountability distinguished the Rashidun from later dynastic rule.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Umar introduced the office of the qadi (judge) in the provinces and instituted the diwan, a register that
questions.A: recorded the marriages and divorces of the Muslims of Madinah each year
questions.B: listed the verses of the Qur'an in the order in which they were revealed
questions.C: recorded the names of Muslims and the stipends paid to them from the treasury
questions.D: counted the camels, horses and weapons of the army before each expedition
questions.explanation: The diwan organised state finances and payments to soldiers and citizens.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Rightly Guided Caliphs ruled in the order
questions.A: Ali, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman
questions.B: Umar, Abu Bakr, Ali, Uthman
questions.C: Abu Bakr, Uthman, Umar, Ali
questions.D: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Ali was assassinated in the mosque of Kufah in 40 AH by
questions.A: Abu Lu'lu'ah, a Persian slave
questions.B: Abdur-Rahman ibn Muljam, a Khariji
questions.C: a soldier of Mu'awiyah
questions.D: a Byzantine spy
questions.explanation: Ibn Muljam struck Ali with a poisoned sword during Fajr.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The first act of the Prophet (SAW) on settling in Madinah was to build a mosque, which served as
questions.A: a fortress against the Quraysh and a store for weapons only
questions.B: a market for the Muhajirun where they traded with the Ansar
questions.C: a place of worship, a school, a court and the seat of government
questions.D: a residence for the Jewish tribes who had accepted the covenant
questions.explanation: The Prophet's mosque was the centre of religious, educational, judicial and political life.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: When Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, an emigrant, was offered half the wealth and one of the wives of his Ansari brother, he declined and asked to be shown the market. This illustrates
questions.A: that trade was forbidden in Madinah during the first years of the Hijrah
questions.B: the refusal of the Ansar to help the emigrants who came from Makkah
questions.C: the poverty of the Ansar, who had nothing to share with the emigrants
questions.D: the self-reliance of the Muhajirun and the generosity of the Ansar
questions.explanation: The brotherhood (mu'akhat) combined generous sharing with dignity and hard work.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Constitution (Sahifah) of Madinah provided that
questions.A: all the Jews of Madinah must convert to Islam within one year or leave the city
questions.B: the Jews and the Muslims formed one community with freedom of religion and joint defence
questions.C: the Quraysh of Makkah would rule Madinah jointly with the Prophet and the Ansar
questions.D: only the Ansar could own land in Madinah and the Muhajirun would work as tenants
questions.explanation: The document recognised religious freedom, mutual defence and the Prophet as final arbiter in disputes.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Munafiqun (hypocrites) of Madinah, led by Abdullah ibn Ubayy,
questions.A: fought bravely at Uhud and were praised by the Prophet for their courage
questions.B: were the Christian tribes of the city who paid the jizyah to the Prophet
questions.C: professed Islam outwardly while secretly working against the Muslims
questions.D: migrated with the Prophet from Makkah and settled among the Ansar
questions.explanation: Ibn Ubayy withdrew 300 men before Uhud and spread slander during the affair of the Ifk.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Suffah was
questions.A: the burial ground of the martyrs of Uhud at the foot of the mountain near Madinah
questions.B: the great market of Madinah where the Muhajirun traded with the Jews and the Ansar
questions.C: the treasury of the Islamic state where the Zakat and the spoils of war were kept
questions.D: a shaded platform in the Prophet's mosque where poor companions devoted to learning lived
questions.explanation: Ahl as-Suffah, including Abu Hurayrah, lived in the mosque and studied under the Prophet.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Jewish tribe expelled from Madinah after breaking the covenant by attempting to assassinate the Prophet (SAW) was
questions.A: Banu Qaynuqa'
questions.B: Banu an-Nadir
questions.C: Banu Qurayzah
questions.D: Banu Hashim
questions.explanation: Banu Qaynuqa' were expelled after Badr, Banu an-Nadir after Uhud, and Banu Qurayzah were judged after the Trench.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The word 'ummah' in the Constitution of Madinah refers to
questions.A: the Ka'bah in Makkah towards which the Muslims turned in prayer after 2 AH
questions.B: the army of the Quraysh that marched against Madinah at Uhud and the Trench
questions.C: the single community formed by the people of Madinah under the Prophet's leadership
questions.D: the clan of Banu Hashim to which the Prophet and his family belonged
questions.explanation: The ummah transcended tribal loyalty and was based on faith and common citizenship.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The economic life of the Muslim community in Madinah was strengthened when the Prophet (SAW)
questions.A: seized the property of the Ansar and divided it among the Muhajirun
questions.B: banned all trade in the city and ordered the Muslims to live only by farming
questions.C: imposed heavy taxes on the farmers of the Ansar to pay for the wars
questions.D: established a Muslim market free from the unfair practices of the existing markets
questions.explanation: He set up a market where no rent was charged and forbade cheating, hoarding and interest.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The brotherhood established between the Muhajirun and the Ansar solved the problem of
questions.A: the shortage of camels and horses for the wars against the Quraysh
questions.B: the emigrants' lack of homes, livelihoods and family support in Madinah
questions.C: the direction of the qiblah before it was changed to the Ka'bah
questions.D: the language barrier between the people of Makkah and Madinah
questions.explanation: The Ansar shared their houses, farms and wealth with the newcomers.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The affair of the Ifk (slander) against A'ishah was ended by
questions.A: a duel between Ali ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Ubayy in the market
questions.B: a decision of the Jewish rabbis of Madinah consulted by the Prophet
questions.C: the revelation of verses in Surah An-Nur declaring her innocence
questions.D: the expulsion of A'ishah from Madinah to her father's house in Makkah
questions.explanation: Surah 24:11-20 cleared A'ishah and prescribed punishment for those who slander chaste women without four witnesses.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Women in the Madinan community participated in public life by
questions.A: being excluded from learning and from every gathering of the Muslims
questions.B: being confined to their houses at all times and never appearing in public
questions.C: serving only as slaves in the houses of the wealthy Ansar and Muhajirun
questions.D: attending the mosque, giving the pledge of allegiance, nursing the wounded and trading
questions.explanation: Women such as Umm Ammarah fought at Uhud, Rufaydah ran a field hospital and A'ishah taught Hadith.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an describes the relationship between husband and wife with the words 'They are a garment for you and you are a garment for them' (2:187). This means spouses should
questions.A: wear the same clothes on Eid days and Fridays
questions.B: protect, comfort and cover each other's faults
questions.C: live in separate houses after the first year
questions.D: compete with each other in earning wealth
questions.explanation: A garment protects, beautifies and conceals; so should each spouse for the other.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (30:21) says Allah created spouses so that you may find tranquillity (sakinah) in them and placed between them
questions.A: fear (khawf) and obedience (ta'ah)
questions.B: wealth (mal) and power (sultan)
questions.C: love (mawaddah) and mercy (rahmah)
questions.D: silence (samt) and distance (bu'd)
questions.explanation: Sakinah, mawaddah and rahmah are the Qur'anic foundations of marriage.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A husband earns a good income but refuses to provide food, clothing and shelter for his wife and children. In Islamic law he
questions.A: is excused because the wife has a job
questions.B: is exercising his right as head of the family
questions.C: is following the Sunnah of frugality
questions.D: has failed in his obligatory duty of nafaqah (maintenance)
questions.explanation: Maintenance of the family is the husband's legal duty even if the wife is wealthy.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam gives the husband the role of qawwam (maintainer and protector) of the family (4:34). This means he should
questions.A: treat his wife as a servant who must obey every command without question
questions.B: take responsibility for the family's welfare with fairness and consultation
questions.C: spend the wife's salary as he likes because he is the head of the family
questions.D: make every decision alone without any discussion with his wife or children
questions.explanation: Qiwamah is responsibility and care, not domination.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Paradise lies at the feet of mothers.' This Hadith stresses
questions.A: that only mothers will enter Paradise on the Day of Judgement
questions.B: that mothers must not work outside the home or earn money
questions.C: the high status of the mother and the duty to serve her
questions.D: that fathers have no rights over their children in Islam
questions.explanation: Serving and pleasing one's mother is a path to Paradise.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The family in Islam is important because it
questions.A: replaces the need for the mosque and the congregational prayers of the Muslims
questions.B: is the only place in which a Muslim is allowed to earn money and own property
questions.C: is forbidden to non-Muslims who live in the lands governed by Islamic law
questions.D: is the basic unit that preserves lineage, morals and the faith of the next generation
questions.explanation: Marriage protects chastity and the family transmits values.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim couple constantly quarrel. The Qur'an (4:35) recommends that in such a case
questions.A: the husband should divorce her at once and marry another woman without delay
questions.B: an arbiter from his family and one from hers should be appointed to reconcile them
questions.C: the wife should return to her parents permanently and never see the husband again
questions.D: the matter should be left to the neighbours to settle in whatever way they wish
questions.explanation: Family arbitration seeks reconciliation before divorce is considered.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam permits a man to marry up to four wives on the condition that he
questions.A: obtains the written permission of the ruler of the state before each marriage
questions.B: is wealthy enough to buy each of them a house and a car of her own
questions.C: deals justly with them; otherwise he should marry only one (4:3)
questions.D: marries all of them on the same day in the presence of the same witnesses
questions.explanation: The verse makes justice the condition and ends: 'if you fear you cannot be just, then one'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A wife in Islam has the right to
questions.A: have her mahr collected and kept by her father as a bride price
questions.B: be denied education by her husband if he considers it unnecessary
questions.C: be married by her father without her consent if he thinks it best
questions.D: own property, keep her earnings and be maintained by her husband
questions.explanation: A Muslim woman retains her legal personality and property after marriage.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim's duties to his relatives (silat ar-rahim) include
questions.A: cutting them off completely if they are poor or in need of help
questions.B: visiting them, helping them in need and maintaining good relations
questions.C: demanding money from them whenever he has a financial problem
questions.D: avoiding them on Eid days so that they will not ask for gifts
questions.explanation: The Prophet said whoever wishes his provision to be increased should keep ties of kinship.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Whoever brings up two daughters till they reach maturity, he and I will come on the Day of Resurrection like this' (joining two fingers). This Hadith
questions.A: forbade the Muslims from having sons or praying for male children
questions.B: commanded that only daughters should be educated and not sons
questions.C: raised the status of daughters in a society that had buried them alive
questions.D: limited every Muslim family to two children and no more than that
questions.explanation: Islam abolished female infanticide and promised reward for raising daughters well.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A household in which the parents pray together with their children, teach them the Qur'an and set a good example illustrates the Qur'anic command
questions.A: 'As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands' (5:38)
questions.B: 'Fight them until there is no persecution and religion is for Allah' (2:193)
questions.C: 'Take not the Jews and the Christians as allies against the believers' (5:51)
questions.D: 'O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire' (66:6)
questions.explanation: Parents are responsible for the religious upbringing of their families.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The dowry (mahr) in Islamic marriage is
questions.A: a payment by the bride's father to the groom
questions.B: a gift the husband must give to the wife, which becomes her own property
questions.C: money given to the imam who conducts the marriage
questions.D: a fee paid to the government
questions.explanation: Qur'an 4:4: 'Give women their dowries as a free gift.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A father forces his adult daughter to marry a man she has rejected. According to the Sunnah,
questions.A: the daughter must accept and remain silent
questions.B: the marriage is valid because the father is her guardian
questions.C: the marriage is invalid without her consent, as the Prophet annulled such a marriage
questions.D: the marriage becomes valid after the wedding feast
questions.explanation: The Prophet annulled the marriage of Khansa' bint Khidham when she complained of being forced.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The essential elements of a valid nikah include
questions.A: the approval of the groom's employer and the imam of the local mosque
questions.B: a large wedding feast with music, dancing and gifts for all the guests
questions.C: registration at a court and the payment of a fee to the government only
questions.D: offer and acceptance, the bride's guardian (wali), two witnesses and the mahr
questions.explanation: Ijab and qabul before two Muslim witnesses with the wali and mahr constitute the contract.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The walimah (wedding feast) is
questions.A: the dowry paid by the husband to the bride at the marriage contract
questions.B: a recommended feast given by the husband to announce the marriage
questions.C: the waiting period observed by a woman after divorce or widowhood
questions.D: the marriage contract itself, concluded before two witnesses
questions.explanation: The Prophet told Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf: 'Give a walimah, even if with one sheep.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim man may not marry
questions.A: a widow whose iddah has already ended
questions.B: a Christian woman from the People of the Book
questions.C: his foster sister who was breastfed by his mother
questions.D: a divorced woman whose iddah has ended
questions.explanation: Fosterage (rada'ah) creates the same prohibitions as blood relationship.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Talaq is disliked (makruh) though permitted. The Prophet (SAW) said:
questions.A: 'A man should divorce three times a year'
questions.B: 'Divorce is the best of all deeds'
questions.C: 'Divorce your wives whenever you like'
questions.D: 'Of all lawful things, the most hateful to Allah is divorce'
questions.explanation: Divorce is a last resort after reconciliation efforts fail.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The iddah (waiting period) of a divorced woman who menstruates is
questions.A: four months and ten days
questions.B: three menstrual cycles
questions.C: one year
questions.D: seven days
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:228; a widow waits four months and ten days; a pregnant woman until delivery.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The purposes of the iddah include
questions.A: allowing the husband to remarry first before the wife is free to do so
questions.B: punishing the wife for the divorce by keeping her away from her family
questions.C: confirming whether the woman is pregnant and giving time for reconciliation
questions.D: collecting the mahr back from the wife before she leaves the house
questions.explanation: The iddah protects lineage and leaves room for the husband to take back his wife in a revocable divorce.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A husband pronounces talaq three times in one sitting in anger. Regarding this practice, Umar ibn al-Khattab
questions.A: ordered the husband to marry another woman immediately as a punishment
questions.B: declared that it was no divorce at all and ordered the couple to stay together
questions.C: imprisoned the wife until the husband agreed to take back his words
questions.D: ruled that it counts as three, to discourage people from abusing divorce
questions.explanation: Umar enforced the triple pronouncement as final to check hasty divorces; earlier it had been treated as one.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: After an irrevocable (final) divorce, the couple may remarry each other only if
questions.A: the husband pays double the original mahr to the wife and her family
questions.B: the woman marries another man, the marriage is consummated and ends naturally
questions.C: one full year passes from the date of the final pronouncement of divorce
questions.D: the wife's father consents in writing before the imam and two witnesses
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:230; the tahlil marriage arranged merely to make her lawful is cursed.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Zihar, the pre-Islamic practice of a husband saying to his wife 'You are to me like my mother's back', is
questions.A: recommended before setting out on Hajj so that the wife remains at home
questions.B: a valid form of divorce that ends the marriage immediately and finally
questions.C: forbidden, and requires expiation before he may resume relations (58:1-4)
questions.D: a form of marriage contract used by the Arabs before and after Islam
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Mujadilah condemns zihar and prescribes freeing a slave, fasting two months or feeding sixty poor.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Marriage in Islam is described in the Qur'an as a 'solemn covenant' (mithaqan ghalizan). This means marriage is
questions.A: a contract that only the husband can end and the wife can never question
questions.B: a temporary arrangement for pleasure that ends whenever one party wishes
questions.C: a business transaction between two families for the exchange of wealth
questions.D: a serious binding contract with rights and duties on both sides
questions.explanation: The description in 4:21 emphasises the gravity of the marital bond.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A woman whose husband disappears or fails to maintain her may seek dissolution of the marriage through
questions.A: a public announcement in the market
questions.B: the court (faskh) on valid grounds
questions.C: returning to her father's house only
questions.D: a fatwa from her friend
questions.explanation: Faskh is judicial annulment on grounds such as desertion, cruelty or failure to maintain.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: The Qur'an pairs the command to worship Allah alone with the command to be kind to parents (17:23). This shows that
questions.A: the rights of parents come before the rights of Allah in every case
questions.B: parents should be worshipped alongside Allah as a sign of gratitude
questions.C: kindness to parents is among the most important duties after Tawhid
questions.D: children have no rights over their parents in the teaching of Islam
questions.explanation: Birr al-walidayn follows immediately after the prohibition of shirk.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: A Muslim's parents, who are non-Muslims, ask him to abandon Islam. The Qur'an (31:15) instructs him to
questions.A: curse them publicly in the mosque and report them to the authorities
questions.B: cut off all contact with them and never speak to them again in his life
questions.C: obey them, leave Islam and return to the religion of his ancestors
questions.D: refuse to obey them in disbelief but still accompany them kindly in this world
questions.explanation: Obedience to parents does not extend to sin, but kindness continues.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: A man asked the Prophet (SAW) for permission to join a military expedition. The Prophet asked if his parents were alive and then said:
questions.A: 'Leave them and go'
questions.B: 'Then strive in their service' (stay and care for them)
questions.C: 'Bring them to fight with you'
questions.D: 'Parents have no rights over a soldier'
questions.explanation: Serving elderly parents is itself a form of jihad.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: Mallam Sani wants to name his newborn son and asks which names Allah loves most. According to the Hadith, the most beloved names to Allah are
questions.A: Harb and Murrah
questions.B: Malik al-Amlak and Shahanshah
questions.C: Abdullah and Abdur-Rahman
questions.D: Abd al-Ka'bah and Abd Shams
questions.explanation: The Prophet said the most beloved names to Allah are Abdullah and Abdur-Rahman; he changed names with bad meanings and forbade names like 'king of kings'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: A father gave a large gift to one son and nothing to his other children, and asked the Prophet (SAW) to witness it. The Prophet said:
questions.A: 'Sell the gift in the market and give me half of the price as charity'
questions.B: 'Give the eldest son everything, for he will care for the others after you'
questions.C: 'Gifts to sons need no fairness; only the daughters must be treated equally'
questions.D: 'Fear Allah and be just among your children; I will not witness injustice'
questions.explanation: The Hadith of Nu'man ibn Bashir establishes equal treatment of children.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: The aqiqah is
questions.A: the circumcision of boys performed on the fortieth day after birth in the presence of the family
questions.B: the sacrifice of a sheep on the seventh day after a child's birth, with shaving of its hair and naming
questions.C: the wedding feast given by the husband on the day after the marriage is consummated
questions.D: the funeral prayer offered for a child who dies before reaching the age of puberty
questions.explanation: Two sheep for a boy and one for a girl are recommended, with charity equal to the weight of the hair in silver.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: Duties of children to their parents after the parents' death include
questions.A: selling their property immediately and dividing the money with friends
questions.B: forgetting them completely and never mentioning their names again
questions.C: praying for them, fulfilling their promises and honouring their friends
questions.D: abandoning their relatives and cutting off all ties with their family
questions.explanation: The Prophet listed these duties when asked whether anything remained of birr after parents die.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: A son speaks rudely to his aged mother and refuses to visit her. In Islam his behaviour is
questions.A: permitted if he is busy
questions.B: acceptable if he sends money
questions.C: a minor mistake with no consequence
questions.D: uquq al-walidayn, one of the major sins
questions.explanation: Disobedience and ill-treatment of parents is counted among the greatest sins after shirk.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: Alhaji Bello feeds and clothes his children well and pays their school fees, but never teaches them to pray, never corrects their bad behaviour and is himself dishonest in business. In Islamic terms he has
questions.A: fulfilled all his duties as a father, since Islam requires only that he provide for their material needs
questions.B: neglected the duty of religious training and good example, which parents owe as much as food
questions.C: done more than Islam requires of a father, since religious training is the duty of the imam and the school
questions.D: no further duty, since a father's responsibility ends once the school fees and feeding are paid for
questions.explanation: The Prophet said: 'It is enough sin for a man to neglect those he is responsible for'; parents owe children religious training and a good example, not only material provision.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: The Qur'an (46:15) describes the mother's role: 'His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship.' This is one reason why the Prophet (SAW)
questions.A: forbade fathers from taking any part in the upbringing of their children
questions.B: excused mothers from the five daily prayers and the fasting of Ramadan
questions.C: gave the mother three times the right to good companionship before the father
questions.D: required mothers to earn the family income while the fathers stayed at home
questions.explanation: The Hadith 'Your mother, your mother, your mother, then your father' recognises her sacrifice.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: A daughter of the Prophet (SAW) whom he would stand up to welcome and seat in his place, and who was called the leader of the women of Paradise, was
questions.A: Umm Kulthum
questions.B: Zaynab
questions.C: Ruqayyah
questions.D: Fatimah
questions.explanation: The Prophet's tenderness towards Fatimah models a father's love and respect for his daughter.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Do not envy one another, do not outbid one another, do not hate one another, do not turn away from one another, and be, O servants of Allah, brothers.' This Hadith forbids
questions.A: trading with non-Muslims in the market
questions.B: envy, hatred and boycotting fellow Muslims
questions.C: attending the mosque for the Friday prayer
questions.D: greeting strangers with the salam
questions.explanation: It lists the social sins that destroy brotherhood and commands the opposite.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim; he does not oppress him, forsake him or despise him.' A student who refuses to help a classmate because he is from another tribe is
questions.A: practising the virtue of taqwa
questions.B: following the Sunnah of the Prophet
questions.C: violating the brotherhood of Islam
questions.D: obeying the command of the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Tribalism (asabiyyah) is condemned; brotherhood is based on faith.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'He is not a believer whose stomach is filled while his neighbour goes hungry.' This teaches
questions.A: that neighbours should be avoided
questions.B: that only Muslims are neighbours
questions.C: that eating is forbidden
questions.D: care and concern for neighbours
questions.explanation: The rights of neighbours include sharing food and preventing harm.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The rights of one Muslim over another, according to the Hadith, include returning the greeting, visiting the sick, following the funeral, accepting invitations and
questions.A: lending money without repayment
questions.B: responding to a sneeze with 'yarhamukallah'
questions.C: sharing one's house permanently
questions.D: paying his Zakat for him
questions.explanation: The Hadith in Muslim lists five or six rights of a Muslim over another.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Backbiting (ghibah) is to mention about your brother what he dislikes.' When asked 'What if it is true?' he said:
questions.A: 'Say it louder so that everyone in the gathering may hear and learn from it'
questions.B: 'Then it is permitted, for the truth may be spoken about anyone at any time'
questions.C: 'If it is true you have backbitten him; if false you have slandered him'
questions.D: 'Only the rich and the powerful may be discussed in their absence'
questions.explanation: Truth does not excuse ghibah; falsehood makes it buhtan (slander).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (49:11-12) forbids mocking others, calling them by offensive nicknames, suspicion, spying and backbiting because these
questions.A: are signs of strong faith
questions.B: are permitted only on Fridays
questions.C: strengthen brotherhood
questions.D: destroy mutual respect and social harmony
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat lays down the etiquette of social relations.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam commands Muslims to spread the greeting of peace (salam) because it
questions.A: is required only between relatives
questions.B: promotes love and brotherhood among people
questions.C: replaces the need for prayer
questions.D: is a sign of wealth
questions.explanation: The Prophet said: 'Spread salam among you and you will love one another.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who is wealthy and hosts lavish parties but never visits his sick neighbour or attends funerals has neglected
questions.A: the rites and rules of the pilgrimage
questions.B: the five pillars of Islam only
questions.C: the social duties of Islamic brotherhood
questions.D: the rules of ablution before prayer
questions.explanation: Visiting the sick and following funerals are rights of Muslims on one another.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Whoever relieves a believer of a hardship of this world, Allah will relieve him of a hardship on the Day of Resurrection.' This encourages
questions.A: hoarding wealth
questions.B: avoiding people in trouble
questions.C: lending at interest
questions.D: helping others in their difficulties
questions.explanation: Mutual assistance is rewarded in the Hereafter.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam's attitude to racism is shown by the Prophet's statement that
questions.A: the Arabs are superior to all other nations because the Qur'an is in Arabic
questions.B: there is no superiority of white over black or black over white except by piety
questions.C: the Quraysh must always rule the Muslims because the Prophet came from them
questions.D: slaves and freed slaves can never be leaders or lead the prayer in the mosque
questions.explanation: Bilal, an Abyssinian former slave, became the first mu'adhdhin; Salman the Persian was called 'one of us'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Reconciling two quarrelling Muslims is described in the Qur'an (49:10) as a duty because
questions.A: one of the two must be a hypocrite who should be exposed
questions.B: quarrels are always about money and property
questions.C: believers are brothers and discord weakens the ummah
questions.D: silence is always better than speaking to either party
questions.explanation: 'So make reconciliation between your brothers and fear Allah.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (5:8) commands: 'Let not the hatred of a people make you swerve from justice. Be just; that is nearer to piety.' A Muslim judge trying a case involving a man who once insulted him should
questions.A: hand it to the man's enemy
questions.B: punish him more severely
questions.C: dismiss the case without hearing
questions.D: judge fairly regardless of his personal feelings
questions.explanation: Justice must not be affected by enmity or friendship.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Umar was sued by a Jew before the judge and the judge stood up to honour the caliph. Umar
questions.A: praised the judge for respecting him and gave him a gift from the treasury
questions.B: rebuked the judge, saying that standing for him was his first act of injustice
questions.C: dismissed the Jew's case at once because a Jew could not sue a Muslim
questions.D: imprisoned the Jew for daring to bring the caliph before a court
questions.explanation: Equality before the law was central to the justice of the Rashidun.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Qur'an 4:58 commands: 'When you judge between people, judge with justice.' A traditional ruler who settles land disputes in favour of whoever pays him most has
questions.A: followed the Sunnah
questions.B: acted within his rights
questions.C: betrayed the trust of judgement
questions.D: shown wisdom
questions.explanation: Bribery in judgement is condemned and its judgement is invalid.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (4:135) commands believers to stand for justice 'even if it be against yourselves, your parents or your relatives, whether rich or poor.' This means that in Islam justice
questions.A: exempts one's own family from testimony and from punishment
questions.B: protects only Muslims and does not extend to non-Muslims
questions.C: favours the poor over the rich in every dispute between them
questions.D: applies equally to all without favour to kin, wealth or status
questions.explanation: Testimony must be truthful even against oneself or one's family.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In the Qur'an (49:9) if two groups of believers fight, others should reconcile them and if one group transgresses, they should fight the transgressor until it returns, then reconcile 'with justice and fairness'. This teaches
questions.A: that Muslims should never intervene in conflicts
questions.B: the duty to restore justice between conflicting parties impartially
questions.C: that the stronger party is always right
questions.D: that war is the first option
questions.explanation: The verse establishes principles of mediation and just settlement.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Ali was caliph when he found his lost coat of armour in the hands of a Christian and took him to the judge Shurayh, who ruled for the Christian because Ali had no witnesses. This shows
questions.A: that judges could be bribed by anyone who had enough money to pay them
questions.B: that Christians were favoured over Muslims in the courts of the caliphate
questions.C: that even the head of state was subject to the law and the rules of evidence
questions.D: that the caliph was above the law and could take whatever he wished
questions.explanation: The Christian was so impressed that he embraced Islam and returned the armour.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Justice (adl) in Islam means
questions.A: obeying the rich and powerful in whatever they command
questions.B: treating friends and relatives better than strangers in every matter
questions.C: punishing the poor severely while pardoning the rich and powerful
questions.D: giving everyone his due and placing things in their right place
questions.explanation: Adl is the opposite of zulm (oppression, putting things in the wrong place).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: An employer pays his Muslim workers promptly but delays the wages of his non-Muslim workers. He has violated the Prophet's command to
questions.A: pay only Muslim workers and leave the non-Muslims to seek their wages in court
questions.B: pay the labourer his wages before his sweat dries, which applies to all workers
questions.C: employ only Muslims in a Muslim's business and dismiss all non-Muslim workers
questions.D: delay all wages until the end of the year so that workers do not leave early
questions.explanation: The right to timely wages is universal in Islamic law.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (16:90) states: 'Indeed, Allah commands justice, good conduct and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality, bad conduct and oppression.' This verse is recited
questions.A: only at funerals before the body is lowered into the grave
questions.B: only during the month of Ramadan in the Tarawih prayers after Isha
questions.C: at the end of every Friday sermon in many mosques as a summary of Islamic ethics
questions.D: only during the Hajj when the pilgrims stand on the plain of Arafat
questions.explanation: Umar ibn Abdul-Aziz introduced its recitation in the khutbah in place of cursing opponents.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Fairness in trade requires a Muslim seller to
questions.A: overcharge strangers who do not know the prices
questions.B: hide the defects of his goods to make a quick sale
questions.C: use two different scales for buying and selling
questions.D: give full measure and weight and disclose defects
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Mutaffifin condemns those who demand full measure but give less.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Islamic principle that a person is innocent until proven guilty and that punishments are averted by doubts (idra'u al-hudud bish-shubuhat) protects
questions.A: criminals from all punishment whatever they have done
questions.B: the accused from unjust punishment on weak evidence
questions.C: only the wealthy who can afford to hire good lawyers
questions.D: only Muslims and not the non-Muslim citizens
questions.explanation: The Prophet said: 'Avert the hudud from the Muslims as much as you can; if there is a way out, let him go.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (4:58) says: 'Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due.' A bank clerk who takes money from customers' accounts has violated
questions.A: hajj (pilgrimage)
questions.B: sawm (fasting)
questions.C: amanah (trust)
questions.D: wudu (ablution)
questions.explanation: Amanah covers money, secrets, positions and duties entrusted to a person.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise; lying leads to wickedness and wickedness leads to the Fire.' A person who tells 'small lies' to escape trouble
