questions.A: is following the Sunnah of the Prophet in difficult situations
questions.B: is doing something permitted since no one is harmed by it
questions.C: earns reward for cleverness in escaping from difficulties
questions.D: is on a path that the Hadith warns leads to wickedness
questions.explanation: Sidq (truthfulness) is a foundation of character; habitual lying leads to being recorded a liar with Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A student finds a wallet containing ₦50,000 and an identity card. The Islamic teaching on luqatah (lost property) requires him to
questions.A: keep it as a gift from Allah since he did not steal it from anyone
questions.B: try to return it to the owner and announce it if the owner is unknown
questions.C: spend it on the mosque immediately without looking for the owner
questions.D: throw it away so that he is not accused of stealing it
questions.explanation: Lost property must be announced for a year (for valuable items) before it may be used, and returned if the owner appears.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'When trust is lost, wait for the Hour.' Asked how it would be lost, he replied: 'When authority is given to those who are not qualified.' This warns against
questions.A: accepting any public office even when one is qualified for it
questions.B: trusting anyone at all in matters of money, property or public office
questions.C: appointing people to positions on the basis of favouritism rather than competence
questions.D: obeying leaders in any matter whether lawful or unlawful
questions.explanation: Placing unqualified people in office is a betrayal of public trust.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A contractor who is paid to build a school with quality materials uses substandard blocks and pockets the difference has committed
questions.A: jihad in the path of Allah (fi sabilillah)
questions.B: an act of sadaqah (voluntary charity)
questions.C: a permissible business practice (tijarah)
questions.D: khiyanah (breach of trust) and ghish (cheating)
questions.explanation: The Prophet said: 'Whoever cheats us is not of us.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'The truthful and trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs.' This Hadith
questions.A: forbids Muslims from engaging in trade
questions.B: gives honest business a very high religious status
questions.C: restricts trade to scholars and their students
questions.D: praises only farmers and not traders
questions.explanation: Honest trade is a form of worship rewarded with the highest company.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: When the Prophet (SAW) passed a heap of grain and found it wet underneath, he asked the seller why he had not put the wet part on top so that people could see it, then said:
questions.A: 'Wet grain is forbidden'
questions.B: 'A good trader hides defects'
questions.C: 'Whoever deceives is not of me'
questions.D: 'Sell it to non-Muslims'
questions.explanation: Concealing defects is forbidden; the buyer has the right to know.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (2:283) says: 'Let the one who is entrusted discharge his trust and fear Allah.' A treasurer of a mosque committee should therefore
questions.A: invest the money in his own business and share the profit with the mosque
questions.B: borrow from the funds without permission and repay when he is able
questions.C: keep the accounts secret from the members so that they do not interfere
questions.D: keep accurate accounts and never use the funds for personal purposes
questions.explanation: Public and religious funds are a sacred trust.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Keeping promises is emphasised in the Qur'an: 'Fulfil the covenant; indeed the covenant will be questioned about' (17:34). A politician who makes promises he never intends to keep
questions.A: is a true believer who trusts in Allah
questions.B: displays the sign of a hypocrite according to the Hadith
questions.C: is following the example of Umar ibn al-Khattab
questions.D: is acting with taqwa and sincerity
questions.explanation: Breaking promises is one of the three marks of nifaq.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: False testimony (shahadat az-zur) is
questions.A: a minor sin that is wiped out by the ablution and the five daily prayers
questions.B: permitted to help a friend or relative who is in trouble with the authorities
questions.C: counted among the greatest sins, mentioned alongside shirk by the Prophet (SAW)
questions.D: allowed in business disputes where the amount of money involved is small
questions.explanation: The Prophet repeated 'and false speech and false witness' until the companions wished he would stop.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Honesty in examinations requires a Muslim student to
questions.A: help his friends by passing answers to them during the examination
questions.B: copy quietly from his neighbour so as not to be caught by the invigilator
questions.C: buy the question paper in advance so that he can prepare the answers
questions.D: rely on his own preparation and refuse to cheat or help others cheat
questions.explanation: Cheating is deception (ghish), which the Prophet condemned.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Allah has cursed the one who gives a bribe and the one who receives it.' An official who demands 'something for the boys' before processing a file has
questions.A: earned a lawful gift
questions.B: incurred the curse mentioned in the Hadith
questions.C: done nothing wrong
questions.D: followed local custom acceptably
questions.explanation: Rishwah (bribery) is condemned whether given or received.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) appointed a man to collect Zakat; he returned saying 'This is for you and this was given to me as a gift.' The Prophet said he should have stayed in his parents' house to see if gifts would come to him. This teaches that
questions.A: Zakat collectors should be rich men who do not need gifts from anyone
questions.B: officials may keep any gifts they receive while carrying out their duties
questions.C: gifts to public officials because of their office belong to the public treasury
questions.D: gifts are always forbidden in Islam whether to officials or to ordinary people
questions.explanation: The Hadith of Ibn al-Lutbiyyah condemns gifts received by virtue of office.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (2:188) says: 'Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, nor use it to bribe judges in order to consume a portion of people's wealth sinfully.' This verse forbids
questions.A: giving charity to judges and their families
questions.B: trade and commerce between Muslims and others
questions.C: inheritance of property by daughters and widows
questions.D: bribery and unlawful acquisition of others' property
questions.explanation: The verse addresses corruption of the judiciary and illegal gain.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Zulm (oppression) in Islam includes
questions.A: praying in congregation in the mosque five times every day with the imam
questions.B: denying people their rights, seizing their property and abusing power over them
questions.C: giving charity to the poor and needy from one's lawful earnings
questions.D: fasting on Mondays and Thursdays as the Prophet used to do
questions.explanation: Oppression is 'darkness on the Day of Resurrection' according to the Hadith.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A governor diverts funds meant for hospitals to his private accounts. Islam classifies this as
questions.A: part of his salary as the governor of the state
questions.B: a lawful allowance for the head of the state
questions.C: ghulul (embezzlement of public property), a grave sin
questions.D: a matter of personal choice with no sin attached
questions.explanation: The Qur'an (3:161) says whoever embezzles will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Umar ibn al-Khattab used to record the wealth of his governors when he appointed them and
questions.A: paid them no salary
questions.B: allowed them to keep whatever they gained
questions.C: never checked their accounts
questions.D: confiscated any unexplained increase when they left office
questions.explanation: Umar's accountability measures prevented officials from enriching themselves.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Hoarding essential goods to create scarcity and profit from people's suffering (ihtikar) is condemned because it
questions.A: increases the wealth of the community
questions.B: oppresses the poor and exploits need
questions.C: is a form of Zakat
questions.D: is encouraged during Ramadan
questions.explanation: The Prophet said: 'No one hoards except a sinner.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an says of Pharaoh that he 'exalted himself in the land and divided its people into factions, oppressing a group among them' (28:4). Modern rulers who oppress their people and sow division are
questions.A: applying the principle of shura in their government
questions.B: practising good governance as Islam requires
questions.C: following the pattern of Pharaoh that the Qur'an condemns
questions.D: obeying the Sunnah of the Prophet in leadership
questions.explanation: The Qur'an holds up Pharaoh as the model of tyranny.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Help your brother whether he is an oppressor or oppressed.' When asked how to help an oppressor, he said:
questions.A: 'By joining him in what he is doing'
questions.B: 'By giving him weapons and men'
questions.C: 'By hiding his crimes from the people'
questions.D: 'By preventing him from oppressing'
questions.explanation: Helping an oppressor means restraining him.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: An employer who underpays his workers and delays their wages while living in luxury is guilty of
questions.A: good management of his business that Islam encourages and rewards
questions.B: oppression that the Prophet (SAW) said Allah will oppose on the Day of Judgement
questions.C: lawful thrift and saving that the Prophet praised in his companions
questions.D: generosity to his family that will be rewarded on the Day of Judgement
questions.explanation: The Hadith Qudsi names among Allah's opponents the one who hires a worker, takes full work and does not pay him.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Nepotism, or appointing unqualified relatives to positions, is contrary to Islam because
questions.A: the Prophet had no relatives whom he could appoint
questions.B: relatives are always dishonest and cannot be trusted
questions.C: positions are trusts to be given to the qualified
questions.D: it is always illegal under the laws of Nigeria
questions.explanation: The Prophet appointed on merit and warned against giving authority to the unqualified.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Islamic response to corruption in public life includes
questions.A: supporting corrupt leaders as long as they are Muslims and attend the Friday prayer regularly
questions.B: silence and acceptance of whatever the leaders do since they were appointed by the will of Allah
questions.C: leaving everything to Allah without any action on the part of the citizens or the scholars
questions.D: accountability of leaders, transparency in public funds and the duty to enjoin good and forbid evil
questions.explanation: Al-amr bil-ma'ruf wan-nahy anil-munkar is a collective duty.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (2:275) says: 'Allah has permitted trade and forbidden riba.' The basic difference between the two is that
questions.A: trade is permitted to Muslims only, while riba is permitted to non-Muslims who live among them
questions.B: in trade risk and effort are shared, while riba is a guaranteed increase on a loan without risk
questions.C: riba involves the exchange of goods, while trade involves only the exchange of money for money
questions.D: trade is forbidden on Fridays and during Ramadan, while riba is forbidden on the other days
questions.explanation: Interest exploits the borrower's need and produces gain without productive effort or risk.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim wants to buy a car but avoid interest. An Islamic bank buys the car and sells it to him at a disclosed profit, payable in instalments. This contract is
questions.A: gharar
questions.B: riba al-fadl
questions.C: murabahah (cost-plus sale)
questions.D: maysir
questions.explanation: Murabahah is a sale at cost plus an agreed mark-up, not a loan with interest.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Two Muslims contribute capital to a business and agree to share profits in a fixed ratio and bear losses in proportion to capital. This partnership is
questions.A: qard hasan
questions.B: mudarabah
questions.C: ijarah
questions.D: musharakah
questions.explanation: In musharakah all partners contribute capital; in mudarabah one provides capital and the other labour.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: An investor provides ₦5 million to a trader who manages the business; profits are shared 60:40 and the investor alone bears financial loss. This arrangement is
questions.A: musharakah
questions.B: mudarabah
questions.C: murabahah
questions.D: istisna'
questions.explanation: Mudarabah (qirad) separates capital provider from entrepreneur; the entrepreneur loses only his effort.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A qard hasan is
questions.A: a gift of money that does not need to be repaid
questions.B: a loan given at a low rate of interest to the poor
questions.C: an interest-free loan repaid without any increase
questions.D: a loan secured on land or a house as collateral
questions.explanation: The 'goodly loan' is praised in the Qur'an (2:245) and rewarded by Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Selling fish still in the river or fruit before it appears on the tree is forbidden because of
questions.A: ijarah (leasing)
questions.B: riba (interest)
questions.C: zakat (charity)
questions.D: gharar (excessive uncertainty)
questions.explanation: Contracts involving unknown or non-existent subject matter are void in Islamic law.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Lotteries, betting on football and gambling machines are forbidden in Islam as
questions.A: sadaqah (charity), which the Qur'an calls a goodly loan
questions.B: maysir (gambling), which the Qur'an calls the work of Satan
questions.C: tijarah (trade), which the Qur'an says Allah has permitted
questions.D: mudarabah (partnership), which the Sunnah encourages
questions.explanation: Qur'an 5:90-91 prohibits maysir because it breeds enmity and diverts from prayer.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam's view of wealth is that
questions.A: it belongs entirely to the individual with no obligations
questions.B: it is evil and should be avoided
questions.C: it belongs to Allah and man is a trustee who must earn and spend it lawfully
questions.D: it should be equally divided among all citizens
questions.explanation: Wealth is a trust (amanah) for which man will be questioned.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islamic law of inheritance requires that
questions.A: the whole estate go to the state treasury to be spent on the poor and needy of the community
questions.B: the eldest son take the whole estate and provide for his mother, brothers and sisters as he sees fit
questions.C: the widow be excluded from the estate and return to her father's house with her children
questions.D: the estate be distributed to fixed heirs in shares laid down in the Qur'an after debts and bequests
questions.explanation: Surah An-Nisa' 4:11-12 and 176 fix the shares of the heirs; bequests are limited to one-third to non-heirs.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Extravagance (israf) and waste (tabdhir) are condemned in the Qur'an, which calls the wasteful
questions.A: the best of creation
questions.B: brothers of the devils (17:27)
questions.C: true believers
questions.D: the people of Paradise
questions.explanation: Moderate spending between miserliness and extravagance is required (25:67).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim businessman pays his workers fairly, does not charge interest, avoids hoarding and pays Zakat. His practice reflects the Islamic economic goal of
questions.A: state ownership of all property so that no individual is richer than another
questions.B: maximum profit at any cost so that the Muslim community becomes wealthy and powerful
questions.C: justice and the circulation of wealth so that it does not remain among the rich only (59:7)
questions.D: the abolition of trade and the return of all Muslims to farming and herding
questions.explanation: The verse on fay' states the principle that wealth should not circulate only among the wealthy.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Waqf (endowment) is
questions.A: the sale of mosque property to raise money for the repair of roads and bridges
questions.B: a loan given to the government by wealthy Muslims to be repaid with a share of the taxes
questions.C: a tax on farmers and herdsmen collected by the state at the time of the harvest
questions.D: dedicating property permanently for charitable or religious purposes so that its benefit continues
questions.explanation: Umar's endowment of land at Khaybar on the Prophet's advice was the first waqf.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: An Islamic principle governing earning is that
questions.A: begging is preferred to work because it teaches humility and dependence on Allah
questions.B: a person should earn through lawful (halal) means and his own effort
questions.C: work is beneath the dignity of a scholar who devotes himself to knowledge
questions.D: wealth from any source is acceptable as long as Zakat is paid on it
questions.explanation: The Prophet said no one eats better food than what he earns by his own hands.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (5:3) lists foods forbidden to Muslims, including
questions.A: dates, honey, olives and the fruits of the trees of Paradise
questions.B: fish, chicken, beef and the milk of camels, cows and goats
questions.C: carrion, blood, pork and animals slaughtered in the name of other than Allah
questions.D: wheat, rice, maize and the grains that grow in the fields of Arabia
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:3 lists the forbidden foods; sea food is lawful (5:96).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: For meat to be halal, the animal must be
questions.A: beaten to death with a club so that the meat becomes soft and tender
questions.B: killed by strangling with a rope so that no blood is spilt on the ground
questions.C: found dead in the field after dying of natural causes or old age
questions.D: slaughtered by cutting the throat with a sharp instrument while mentioning Allah's name
questions.explanation: Dhabh requires severing the throat, windpipe and jugular veins with the tasmiyah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim doctor prescribes a medicine containing alcohol when no alternative exists and the patient's life is in danger. Islamic law
questions.A: forbids it absolutely even if the patient dies, since alcohol is haram in every situation
questions.B: permits the necessary amount under the principle that necessity makes the forbidden permissible
questions.C: requires the patient to fast for sixty days instead of taking the medicine that contains alcohol
questions.D: treats it as a major sin for which the doctor and the patient must both seek forgiveness
questions.explanation: Ad-darurat tubih al-mahzurat, subject to taking only what is necessary.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following occupations is unlawful (haram) for a Muslim?
questions.A: working as a teacher in a secondary school
questions.B: working as a farmer on a rice plantation
questions.C: working as a cashier in a gambling house
questions.D: working as a nurse in a general hospital
questions.explanation: Earning from gambling, alcohol, interest or fraud is unlawful even if the worker does not consume the product.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Interest received from a conventional bank savings account is
questions.A: a lawful profit earned on the customer's savings
questions.B: a lawful gift from the bank to its customers
questions.C: Zakat paid by the bank on behalf of the customer
questions.D: riba, which must not be used for personal benefit
questions.explanation: Scholars advise disposing of such interest to the poor without expecting reward.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islamic dress requirements for both men and women are based on the principle of
questions.A: wearing only white
questions.B: modesty (haya') and covering the awrah
questions.C: wearing only Arab clothing
questions.D: wearing expensive garments
questions.explanation: Surah An-Nur 24:30-31 commands both sexes to lower their gaze and guard modesty.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim is unsure whether the meat sold in a particular shop is halal. The Prophet's guidance is to
questions.A: eat it if it is cheap and leave it if it is expensive
questions.B: eat it and say Bismillah before the first bite
questions.C: leave what causes doubt for what does not cause doubt
questions.D: eat it only on Fridays after the Jumu'ah prayer
questions.explanation: The Hadith 'leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not' guides such cases.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Zina (fornication and adultery) is forbidden in the Qur'an with the words 'Do not approach zina' (17:32). The phrase 'do not approach' means that
questions.A: it is a minor sin that is forgiven by the ablution and the daily prayers
questions.B: only the act itself is forbidden and everything leading to it is permitted
questions.C: it is permitted for unmarried people and forbidden only for the married
questions.D: even the steps leading to it, such as immodest mixing, are to be avoided
questions.explanation: Islam blocks the means (sadd adh-dhara'i') that lead to major sins.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following is lawful (halal) in Islam?
questions.A: selling alcohol to non-Muslims
questions.B: trade in goods bought and sold openly at agreed prices
questions.C: lending money at 5 per cent interest
questions.D: selling stolen goods cheaply
questions.explanation: Honest trade is lawful; the others involve haram substances, riba or theft.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Drugs such as cannabis and tramadol abuse are forbidden by analogy (qiyas) with
questions.A: gambling (maysir), because every game played for money is the work of Satan
questions.B: pork (khinzir), because every animal that is not slaughtered is haram to eat
questions.C: khamr (intoxicants), because 'every intoxicant is khamr and every khamr is haram'
questions.D: carrion (maytah), because every dead thing is impure and haram to touch
questions.explanation: The Hadith extends the prohibition to all intoxicating substances.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (7:157) describes the Prophet as one who 'makes lawful for them the good things and forbids them the evil things'. This indicates that Islamic prohibitions
questions.A: were meant for a limited time and no longer apply
questions.B: are arbitrary and have no purpose that can be understood
questions.C: apply only to the Arabs and not to other nations
questions.D: are for the benefit and protection of human beings
questions.explanation: Every prohibition guards life, faith, intellect, lineage or property.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Halal earnings are important because the Prophet (SAW) said that Allah does not accept the prayer of one whose
questions.A: clothes are old and patched in several places
questions.B: food, drink and clothing are from haram sources
questions.C: house is small and built of mud and thatch
questions.D: income is modest and barely feeds his family
questions.explanation: The Hadith describes a traveller raising his hands in du'a while nourished by haram: 'how can he be answered?'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The head of the Islamic state after the Prophet (SAW) was called the khalifah, meaning
questions.A: priest of the mosque who leads the prayers and sermons
questions.B: king with absolute power over life and property
questions.C: successor or deputy who rules according to the Shari'ah
questions.D: commander of the navy in the Mediterranean Sea
questions.explanation: The caliph succeeded the Prophet in leading the community, not in receiving revelation.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In Abu Bakr's inaugural speech he said: 'The weak among you is strong with me until I restore his right to him, and the strong among you is weak with me until I take the right from him.' This expresses the principle of
questions.A: military dictatorship
questions.B: the superiority of the Quraysh
questions.C: hereditary succession
questions.D: equal justice for all under the rule of law
questions.explanation: The speech is a charter of accountable, just leadership.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Bayt al-Mal in the Islamic state was
questions.A: the house of the caliph in Madinah where he received delegations from the provinces
questions.B: the public treasury that received Zakat, kharaj, jizyah and spoils and paid public expenses
questions.C: the central mosque of the capital where the caliph led the Friday prayer and sermon
questions.D: the army barracks outside the city where the soldiers lived with their families
questions.explanation: Umar organised the treasury with registers and regular stipends.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Kharaj was
questions.A: the Zakat paid by the Muslims on their gold and silver
questions.B: the poll tax paid by non-Muslim men of the state
questions.C: a land tax paid on agricultural land in conquered territories
questions.D: a tax paid on goods brought into the markets
questions.explanation: Kharaj on land and jizyah on non-Muslim adult males were major sources of state revenue.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The jizyah paid by non-Muslim citizens (dhimmis) of the Islamic state was in return for
questions.A: protection by the state and exemption from military service
questions.B: the right to build churches and synagogues only
questions.C: a share in the spoils of war captured by the Muslim armies
questions.D: the right to marry Muslim women and inherit from them
questions.explanation: Dhimmis were protected people; Umar returned the jizyah when he could not protect Syrian towns.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Umar divided the empire into provinces, each under a wali (governor), and required governors to
questions.A: attend the Hajj yearly where complaints against them could be heard
questions.B: pay him a personal tribute from the taxes of their provinces each year
questions.C: rule their provinces without any supervision from the capital in Madinah
questions.D: keep the taxes of their provinces for themselves and their families
questions.explanation: The Hajj served as an annual assembly for accountability.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The hisbah in the Islamic state was the office responsible for
questions.A: supervising markets, weights and measures, and public morality
questions.B: leading the army in the wars against the Persians and the Byzantines
questions.C: collecting the jizyah from the non-Muslim citizens of the state
questions.D: teaching the Qur'an to the children of the Muslims in the mosques
questions.explanation: The muhtasib enforced fair trading and prevented public wrongs.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) sent Mu'adh ibn Jabal to Yemen as governor and judge and asked how he would judge. Mu'adh replied: by the Qur'an, then the Sunnah, then
questions.A: his own reasoning (ijtihad) without negligence
questions.B: the customs of the Yemenis before Islam
questions.C: the opinion of the Persian governors of Yemen
questions.D: casting lots to find the answer
questions.explanation: The Prophet approved, establishing the sources of law and the place of ijtihad.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Sovereignty in an Islamic political system belongs to
questions.A: Allah, whose law the rulers and the ruled must follow
questions.B: the caliph, whose word is law and cannot be questioned
questions.C: the army, which chooses and removes the caliph
questions.D: the wealthy merchants, who pay the taxes of the state
questions.explanation: Hakimiyyah belongs to Allah; the ruler implements the Shari'ah as a trustee.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The bay'ah (pledge of allegiance) given to a caliph represents
questions.A: a contract in which the people agree to obey him so long as he rules by the Shari'ah
questions.B: an unconditional submission for life that cannot be withdrawn for any reason whatever
questions.C: a payment of tax made by the people to the caliph at the beginning of his reign
questions.D: a military oath taken by the soldiers only and not by the ordinary citizens
questions.explanation: Obedience is conditional: 'no obedience to a creature in disobedience to the Creator'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Under the Rightly Guided Caliphs, judges (qadis) were
questions.A: independent and could rule against the caliph himself
questions.B: appointed only from the caliph's family
questions.C: forbidden to hear cases against officials
questions.D: paid by the litigants
questions.explanation: Umar's letter to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari set out the principles of impartial judging.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Umar declined to distribute the conquered lands of Iraq among the soldiers and instead left them with their cultivators subject to kharaj, because
questions.A: future generations of Muslims would need revenue and the land should benefit all
questions.B: the soldiers refused to accept the land and asked for money and slaves instead
questions.C: the land was infertile and could not be cultivated by the Arab soldiers
questions.D: the Persian nobles demanded it as a condition of their surrender to the Muslims
questions.explanation: Umar cited Surah Al-Hashr 59:10 on those who would come after.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an describes the believers as those 'whose affair is conducted by mutual consultation' (42:38). Shura means that
questions.A: leaders should consult the people and the knowledgeable before deciding
questions.B: the leader decides every matter alone and the people must accept his decision
questions.C: only the commanders of the army are consulted before any decision is taken
questions.D: decisions are made by casting lots after the leader has prayed for guidance
questions.explanation: The Prophet was commanded 'consult them in affairs' (3:159) though he received revelation.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: At the battle of the Trench, the Prophet (SAW) considered giving a third of Madinah's harvest to the Ghatafan to make them withdraw, but dropped the plan when
questions.A: the Ansar leaders Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn Ubadah objected after being consulted
questions.B: the Quraysh attacked across the trench and the Muslims had to fight them off
questions.C: the Jewish tribe of Banu Qurayzah agreed to pay the Ghatafan from their own wealth
questions.D: a revelation came down forbidding the payment of any tribute to the enemy
questions.explanation: He respected the view of those consulted, illustrating genuine shura.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A qualification for leadership in Islam illustrated by the Qur'anic story of Talut (Saul) is
questions.A: knowledge and physical ability rather than wealth
questions.B: wealth and noble birth rather than knowledge
questions.C: old age and long experience rather than strength
questions.D: membership of a ruling family rather than ability
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:247: Allah chose him and increased him in knowledge and stature.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Umar said: 'Whoever pledges allegiance to a man without consultation of the Muslims, neither he nor the one he pledged to is to be followed.' This shows that in Islam legitimate leadership requires
questions.A: the consent and consultation of the community
questions.B: military conquest of the capital city
questions.C: inheritance from the previous ruler's family
questions.D: great wealth and the support of the merchants
questions.explanation: Bay'ah based on shura legitimises authority.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Whoever obeys the amir has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the amir has disobeyed me,' but also said 'There is no obedience in sin.' Together these teach that
questions.A: obedience to rulers is required in lawful matters only
questions.B: rulers must be obeyed in everything they command
questions.C: rulers should never be obeyed by a true believer
questions.D: only the Prophet may be obeyed and no one else
questions.explanation: Obedience is conditional on the ruler's command being lawful.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In his letter appointing a governor, Ali advised him to choose as judges the best of his people and to pay them generously so that
questions.A: they would not be tempted by bribes
questions.B: they would fight in the army
questions.C: they would praise the caliph
questions.D: they would collect more taxes
questions.explanation: Ali's letter to Malik al-Ashtar is a classic on just administration.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Leadership qualities required of an Islamic leader include
questions.A: piety, justice, knowledge, courage and consultation
questions.B: wealth, lineage and eloquence only
questions.C: military strength alone
questions.D: popularity on social media
questions.explanation: The Prophet and the Rashidun combined taqwa with competence.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: When a governor appointed by Umar was found to have built a palace with a gate that kept out the poor, Umar
questions.A: ordered the gate to be burnt so that the people could reach their governor
questions.B: praised his good taste and sent him more money to complete the palace
questions.C: gave him a larger province as a reward for building such a fine palace
questions.D: ignored the complaint because a governor may live as he pleases
questions.explanation: Accessibility of leaders to the people is a duty of leadership.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'When three set out on a journey, let them appoint one of them as leader.' This teaches that
questions.A: organised leadership is necessary in every group activity
questions.B: travelling in groups of three is discouraged in Islam
questions.C: the eldest member of any group must always be its leader
questions.D: leadership is needed only in times of war and danger
questions.explanation: Even a small group needs an amir for order and decision-making.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Accountability of leaders in Islam is shown by Umar's statement:
questions.A: 'If a mule stumbles in Iraq, I fear Allah will ask me why I did not pave the road for it'
questions.B: 'The state and everything in it belong to me and my family after me for ever'
questions.C: 'The people exist to serve the caliph and the caliph answers only to himself'
questions.D: 'I answer to no one for what I do, since Allah has placed me over you all'
questions.explanation: Umar felt responsible for every subject and even every animal.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Ahl al-Hall wal-Aqd in Islamic political thought are
questions.A: the representatives and people of knowledge and influence who choose and advise the ruler
questions.B: the soldiers of the caliph's personal guard who protect him and carry out his orders
questions.C: the slaves and servants of the palace who attend to the caliph and his family
questions.D: the traders of Makkah and Madinah who pay the largest share of the taxes
questions.explanation: 'Those who loosen and bind' exercised shura on behalf of the community.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A school prefect consults his classmates before setting rules for the class and accepts the majority view. He is practising
questions.A: shura
questions.B: zulm
questions.C: riba
questions.D: ghibah
questions.explanation: Shura applies to homes, schools and associations as well as the state.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (60:8) says Allah does not forbid Muslims from dealing kindly and justly with those who have not fought them because of religion nor driven them from their homes. This means Muslims should
questions.A: treat peaceful non-Muslims with kindness and justice
questions.B: avoid all contact with non-Muslims in every situation
questions.C: fight all non-Muslims until they accept Islam
questions.D: trade only with Muslims and boycott all others
questions.explanation: Birr (kindness) and qist (justice) are owed to peaceful non-Muslims.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Whoever harms a dhimmi (non-Muslim under protection), I will be his opponent on the Day of Judgement.' This shows that
questions.A: the rights of non-Muslim citizens are protected in Islam
questions.B: non-Muslims have no rights
questions.C: only Muslims may live in a Muslim state
questions.D: harming non-Muslims is rewarded
questions.explanation: Protected non-Muslims enjoyed security of life, property and worship.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) stood up as a funeral procession passed and, when told it was a Jew, said:
questions.A: 'Is it not a human soul?'
questions.B: 'Then sit down'
questions.C: 'Do not honour him'
questions.D: 'Curse him'
questions.explanation: Respect for human dignity extends to non-Muslims.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) accepted gifts from the Negus and the ruler of Egypt (Muqawqis), and pawned his armour with a Jew for food. This shows that
questions.A: peaceful economic and social dealings with non-Muslims are permitted
questions.B: the Prophet trusted only Muslims and dealt with others out of necessity
questions.C: trade with non-Muslims is haram except in times of famine and war
questions.D: Muslims may not accept gifts from anyone who is not a Muslim
questions.explanation: The Sunnah demonstrates normal relations of trade, gifts and neighbourliness.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim's non-Muslim neighbour is sick. According to the Sunnah the Muslim should
questions.A: visit him and show him kindness
questions.B: ignore him
questions.C: move house
questions.D: refuse to greet his family
questions.explanation: The Prophet visited a sick Jewish boy who served him and invited him to Islam gently.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam permits Muslim men to marry chaste women from the People of the Book (5:5). This indicates that
questions.A: family ties with Jews and Christians are lawful within the rules of the Shari'ah
questions.B: marriage with any non-Muslim is forbidden to both Muslim men and Muslim women
questions.C: Christian women must convert to Islam before a Muslim man may marry them
questions.D: the wife must be enslaved and her children raised without any religion
questions.explanation: The permission implies respect and lawful relations with the Ahl al-Kitab.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (16:125) commands: 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best.' Da'wah to non-Muslims should therefore be
questions.A: wise, gentle and respectful
questions.B: forceful and threatening
questions.C: insulting to their beliefs
questions.D: conducted only by scholars
questions.explanation: Force and abuse are contrary to the Qur'anic method of da'wah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an (6:108) forbids Muslims from insulting the gods of the polytheists because
questions.A: they would insult Allah in return out of ignorance
questions.B: all gods are equal and deserve the same respect
questions.C: insulting their gods is a form of da'wah that is not effective
questions.D: the polytheists are always right in what they believe
questions.explanation: The verse protects mutual respect and prevents provoking blasphemy.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Christian delegation of Najran signed a treaty with the Prophet (SAW) that
questions.A: guaranteed the protection of their lives, property, churches and religious practice
questions.B: required them to convert to Islam within one year or leave the Arabian peninsula
questions.C: banned them from entering Arabia and trading with the Muslims of Madinah
questions.D: confiscated their churches and turned them into mosques for the Muslims
questions.explanation: The treaty is a model of religious tolerance.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In a multi-religious country like Nigeria, the Islamic principle that best guides Muslim-Christian relations is
questions.A: peaceful coexistence with justice, kindness and freedom of religion
questions.B: forced conversion of the Christians to Islam by the Muslim majority
questions.C: separation of the two communities into different regions of the country
questions.D: refusal to cooperate with Christians on any matter, religious or worldly
questions.explanation: 'There is no compulsion in religion' and 'to you your religion and to me mine' underpin coexistence.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) allowed the Jews of Madinah to be judged by their own law in their disputes. This shows
questions.A: respect for the religious autonomy of non-Muslim communities
questions.B: that Muslim law did not exist
questions.C: that Jews were superior
questions.D: that the Prophet did not care about justice
questions.explanation: The Constitution of Madinah recognised communal autonomy.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The battle of Badr was significant because
questions.A: it was the first decisive victory that established the Muslims as a power in Arabia
questions.B: the Muslims were heavily defeated and lost seventy of their best fighters
questions.C: the Prophet was killed and the Muslims had to choose a new leader
questions.D: it took place in Makkah and led to the immediate conquest of the city
questions.explanation: Badr (2 AH) is called Yawm al-Furqan, the day of the criterion.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: At the battle of Uhud, the Prophet (SAW) was wounded and a rumour spread that he had been killed. The main cause of the setback was that
questions.A: the archers left their position on the hill to collect spoils against orders
questions.B: the Muslims had no weapons and had to fight the Quraysh with sticks and stones
questions.C: the Ansar refused to fight and returned to Madinah before the battle began
questions.D: the Muslims outnumbered the enemy and became careless and overconfident
questions.explanation: Khalid ibn al-Walid's cavalry attacked from the rear when the archers abandoned the pass.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (6 AH) provided for
questions.A: a ten-year truce and permission for the Muslims to perform Umrah the following year
questions.B: the immediate surrender of Makkah and the handing over of the keys of the Ka'bah
questions.C: the expulsion of the Muslims from Madinah and their return to Makkah as subjects
questions.D: the payment of a yearly tribute by the Quraysh to the Muslims of Madinah
questions.explanation: The peace allowed Islam to spread rapidly; within two years more people accepted Islam than in the previous nineteen.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Quraysh violated the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah by
questions.A: helping Banu Bakr attack Banu Khuza'ah, allies of the Muslims
questions.B: refusing to allow the caravans of Madinah to trade in the markets of Makkah
questions.C: attacking the Muslims at Uhud and killing seventy of the companions
questions.D: killing the Negus of Abyssinia who had given refuge to the Muslims
questions.explanation: This breach led to the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Makkah was conquered in 8 AH
questions.A: almost without bloodshed, and the Prophet destroyed the idols in the Ka'bah
questions.B: after a long siege and heavy fighting in which thousands of Makkans were killed
questions.C: by the Persian army, which then handed the city over to the Muslims
questions.D: before the battle of Badr, which was fought to defend the newly won city
questions.explanation: The Prophet entered peacefully, cleansed the Ka'bah of 360 idols and forgave the Makkans.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The expedition to Tabuk (9 AH) was directed against
questions.A: the Byzantines on the Syrian frontier
questions.B: the Persians on the frontier of Iraq
questions.C: the Quraysh on the road to Makkah
questions.D: the Jews of Khaybar north of Madinah
questions.explanation: Tabuk was the last expedition led by the Prophet; the enemy did not appear.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Under Caliph Umar, the Muslim armies defeated the Byzantines at Yarmuk and the Persians at
questions.A: Qadisiyyah and Nahavand
questions.B: Badr and Uhud
questions.C: Siffin and the Camel
questions.D: Khaybar and Hunayn
questions.explanation: Qadisiyyah (636) and Nahavand (642) ended the Sasanian empire.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Egypt was conquered for the Muslims under Umar by
questions.A: Amr ibn al-As
questions.B: Khalid ibn al-Walid
questions.C: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas
questions.D: Abu Ubaydah
questions.explanation: Amr ibn al-As founded the city of Fustat; Khalid and Abu Ubaydah led in Syria, Sa'd in Iraq.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Umayyad dynasty, which followed the Rightly Guided Caliphs, was founded by
questions.A: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, with its capital at Damascus
questions.B: Abu al-Abbas, with its capital at Baghdad
questions.C: Uthman ibn Affan
questions.D: Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf
questions.explanation: Mu'awiyah became sole ruler in 41 AH and introduced hereditary succession.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Abbasid caliphate, with its capital at Baghdad, is remembered for
questions.A: the flourishing of learning, translation and science, including the Bayt al-Hikmah
questions.B: the conquest of Spain and the founding of the great mosque of Cordoba
questions.C: the first compilation of the Qur'an into a single book after the Prophet's death
questions.D: the battle of Badr and the first great victory of the Muslims over the Quraysh
questions.explanation: Under Harun ar-Rashid and al-Ma'mun Baghdad became the intellectual centre of the world.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam spread into Spain (al-Andalus) in 711 CE under
questions.A: Tariq ibn Ziyad
questions.B: Uqbah ibn Nafi
questions.C: Salahuddin
questions.D: Amr ibn al-As
questions.explanation: Tariq crossed the strait that bears his name (Gibraltar) and defeated the Visigoths.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam entered North Africa and spread across the Sahara to West Africa mainly through
questions.A: trade caravans and the activities of Muslim merchants and scholars
questions.B: the Crusades fought between the Christians and the Muslims of Palestine
questions.C: the conquest of Spain by the armies of Tariq ibn Ziyad and Musa ibn Nusayr
questions.D: the Byzantine army which carried the religion to the peoples of Africa
questions.explanation: Trans-Saharan traders and Berber clerics brought Islam to Ghana, Mali, Kanem and Hausaland.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The ruler of Mali whose pilgrimage to Makkah in 1324 displayed the wealth of West African Islam was
questions.A: Mansa Musa
questions.B: Askia Muhammad
questions.C: Usman dan Fodio
questions.D: Mai Idris Alooma
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's Hajj spread Mali's fame and he brought scholars and architects back to Timbuktu.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam is believed to have reached Kanem-Bornu around the eleventh century, and by the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries it had spread to the Hausa states through
questions.A: Wangara (Dyula) traders and scholars from Mali
questions.B: Portuguese sailors
questions.C: the Sokoto Jihad
questions.D: the British colonial administration
questions.explanation: Islam reached Kano under Sarki Yaji in the fourteenth century via Wangara traders.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Sokoto Jihad (1804-1808) led by Shehu Usman dan Fodio resulted in
questions.A: the establishment of the Sokoto Caliphate over most of Hausaland
questions.B: the end of Islam in Northern Nigeria and the return of traditional religion
questions.C: the conquest of Lagos and the coastal towns of Yorubaland by the Fulani
questions.D: the founding of Ibadan as the capital of a new Muslim empire in the south
questions.explanation: The caliphate, with its capital at Sokoto, reformed religious practice and governance.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The daughter of Usman dan Fodio who was a renowned scholar, poet and educator of women was
questions.A: Nana Asma'u
questions.B: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid
questions.C: Aminah of Zazzau
questions.D: Hafsah bint Umar
questions.explanation: Nana Asma'u organised the Yan Taru movement to educate women in rural areas.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam spread in Yorubaland before the nineteenth century mainly through
questions.A: Muslim traders and clerics from the north, giving rise to the term 'Imale'
questions.B: the Sokoto Jihad's direct conquest of Lagos and the Yoruba coastal towns
questions.C: Portuguese missionaries who came to Lagos and Badagry by sea from Europe
questions.D: the officers of the Royal Niger Company who governed the region for Britain
questions.explanation: Yoruba Muslims were called Imale (people of Mali), pointing to the northern trade route.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Crusades were
questions.A: European military expeditions to seize Jerusalem and the Holy Land from Muslim rule
questions.B: Muslim conquests of the cities of Europe led by the Umayyad caliphs of Spain
questions.C: trade agreements between the caliphs of Baghdad and the popes of Rome
questions.D: pilgrimages to Makkah made by the Christians of Europe during the Middle Ages
questions.explanation: Salahuddin al-Ayyubi retook Jerusalem in 1187 and treated its inhabitants mercifully.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The battle of Khaybar (7 AH) resulted in
questions.A: the Jews of Khaybar keeping their land as tenants in return for half the produce
questions.B: the destruction of Madinah by the Jewish tribes and their allies from Makkah
questions.C: the death of the Prophet from wounds received in the fighting around the forts
questions.D: the conversion of all the Jews of Khaybar to Islam on the day of the battle
questions.explanation: The arrangement (musaqah) was an early example of agricultural partnership.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Ottoman Empire, which ruled much of the Muslim world for six centuries, ended with the abolition of the caliphate in
questions.explanation: The Ottoman caliphate was abolished by the Turkish republic in 1924; Baghdad fell to the Mongols in 1258; Granada fell in 1492.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim youth is encouraged by friends to join a group that attacks schools and kidnaps girls in the name of religion. The Islamic position is that
questions.A: such acts are terrorism and oppression forbidden by the Qur'an, and he must refuse
questions.B: any group that claims to be fighting for Islam must be obeyed and supported by Muslims
questions.C: violence is permitted against non-Muslims as long as it is done in the name of religion
questions.D: kidnapping girls is a form of jihad that will be rewarded on the Day of Judgement
questions.explanation: Killing innocents, attacking places of learning and enslaving free people violate Islamic law.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Seeking knowledge is an obligation on every Muslim.' A father who refuses to send his daughters to school on religious grounds
questions.A: contradicts the Sunnah, which obliges both males and females to seek knowledge
questions.B: is following Islamic teaching, which limits education to the male members of the family
questions.C: is protecting his daughters as Islam demands by keeping them away from strangers
questions.D: is exempt from the duty of educating them because they will marry and leave the home
questions.explanation: A'ishah and Nana Asma'u were scholars; Islam obliges education for all.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: HIV/AIDS prevention from an Islamic perspective emphasises
questions.A: chastity before marriage and faithfulness within it, together with compassion for the sick
questions.B: isolation and public condemnation of patients so that others will fear the disease
questions.C: that the disease affects only non-Muslims and those who do not attend the mosque
questions.D: that medical treatment of the disease is forbidden because it is a punishment from Allah
questions.explanation: Islam prohibits zina and commands care for the sick without stigma.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam's teaching on the environment is that man is a khalifah (steward) on earth and that
questions.A: wastefulness, pollution and needless destruction of trees and animals are forbidden
questions.B: man may exploit the resources of nature without any limit since they were made for him
questions.C: animals and plants have no rights and may be treated in whatever way man wishes
questions.D: planting trees and protecting forests is a waste of time that brings no reward
questions.explanation: The Prophet forbade cutting trees needlessly and said planting a tree from which any creature eats is charity.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who is offered a job requiring him to falsify company accounts should
questions.A: refuse, because obedience to an employer does not extend to sin
questions.B: accept the job in order to support his family and pray for forgiveness
questions.C: accept the job but pay Zakat on the salary to purify the income
questions.D: accept the job on condition that he is not the one who signs the accounts
questions.explanation: Halal earning is a duty; there is no obedience in sin.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The rise of drug abuse among youths is addressed in Islam by
questions.A: the prohibition of all intoxicants and the promotion of self-discipline and good company
questions.B: allowing drugs in moderation as long as the user does not miss the daily prayers
questions.C: ignoring the problem since it affects only those who have left the religion
questions.D: banning young people from the mosque until they have given up the habit completely
questions.explanation: Qur'an 5:90 and the Hadith on intoxicants apply to hard drugs; the Prophet warned about the influence of companions.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam's position on the abuse of social media through rumour, insult and pornography is based on the Qur'anic commands to
questions.A: verify news, guard the tongue and lower the gaze
questions.B: post as many messages as possible every day
questions.C: share every message received with all one's contacts
questions.D: insult those who disagree with one's opinions
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat and Surah An-Nur provide the ethics of communication and modesty.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Female genital mutilation (FGM) is practised in some Muslim communities. The correct Islamic position is that
questions.A: harming the body is forbidden ('no harm and no reciprocating harm') and FGM has no basis in the Qur'an
questions.B: FGM is one of the pillars of Islam and every Muslim girl must undergo it before the age of puberty
questions.C: FGM is required by Islamic law before a woman may be married under a valid nikah contract
questions.D: FGM was commanded by the Prophet in the Farewell Sermon as a duty on every Muslim family
questions.explanation: Many scholars and Al-Azhar have condemned FGM as a harmful custom, not a religious obligation.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Ethnic and religious violence in Nigeria contradicts the Qur'anic teaching that Allah made mankind into nations and tribes
questions.A: 'that you may know one another' (49:13), not that you may despise one another
questions.B: so that the strongest tribe may rule over the weaker tribes and nations
questions.C: so that the Arabs may lead all the other nations of the world for ever
questions.D: to keep them apart permanently so that they never mix or intermarry
questions.explanation: Diversity is for mutual knowledge; nobility lies in taqwa.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A wealthy Muslim politician spends millions on a lavish wedding while his community lacks clean water. Islam would describe his spending as
questions.A: israf (extravagance), while neglecting the rights of the needy
questions.B: praiseworthy generosity that will be rewarded in Paradise
questions.C: a form of Zakat that purifies the rest of his wealth
questions.D: the Sunnah of the Prophet at the weddings of his daughters
questions.explanation: The Prophet's own daughter's wedding was simple; extravagance amid need is condemned.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Islamic approach to poverty alleviation includes
questions.A: Zakat, sadaqah, waqf, interest-free loans and the dignity of work
questions.B: begging as a respectable career for those who cannot find employment
questions.C: gambling and lotteries as a way for the poor to win money quickly
questions.D: hoarding food in times of plenty so that it can be sold when prices rise
questions.explanation: These institutions redistribute wealth and empower the poor.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Examination malpractice, cultism and internet fraud ('yahoo yahoo') are all condemned in Islam under the general prohibitions of
questions.A: deception, oppression and consuming people's wealth unjustly
questions.B: trade, commerce and the lending of money
questions.C: travel, migration and living in a foreign land
questions.D: study, reading and the use of the internet
questions.explanation: 'Whoever cheats us is not of us' and 'do not consume one another's wealth unjustly' (4:29).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Islamic view of organ donation to save a life is, according to most contemporary scholars,
questions.A: permissible under conditions, because saving a life is like saving all mankind (5:32)
questions.B: absolutely forbidden, because the body belongs to Allah and may not be cut for any reason
questions.C: compulsory for all Muslims, who must register as donors before performing the Hajj
questions.D: allowed only when the organ is sold, so that the donor's family receives compensation
questions.explanation: Most fiqh councils allow donation that does not harm the donor and is not sold.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In dealing with a global pandemic, the Hadith 'If you hear of a plague in a land, do not enter it; and if it breaks out where you are, do not leave' supports
questions.A: quarantine and public health measures
questions.B: ignoring medical advice
questions.C: travelling freely to spread comfort
questions.D: closing all hospitals
questions.explanation: The Prophet's guidance anticipates modern quarantine practice.
